News.title: Arsenal maintain perfect start but lack firepower of rivals
News.content:
Bukayo Saka maintained Arsenal’s perfect start to the season, but Mikel Arteta appeared to acknowledge that the Premier League champions are in danger of leaving themselves short in attack.

There is still time for Arteta to add another forward to his squad and whether he does so or not could be important, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday night.

Having sold Leandro Trossard and with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus on the verge of moves away, Arsenal appear light of forward options.

Lyon winger Malick Fofana has been offered to the club, but he is an underwhelming target given Morgan Rogers and Vinícius Júnior were pursued earlier in the summer.

“We are trying to improve the squad,” Arteta, the Arsenal head coach, said. “Until Tuesday night, we’re going to try to do that. I’ve been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match. I will give it [my energy] now.”

Asked if he currently has enough depth in forward positions, Arteta added: “It depends if everybody is fit or not. We know that the depth has to be really big when you are fighting for four competitions. So we’re going to try to do that.”

News.title: Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season
News.content:
Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

Sports.title: Arsenal ‘made approach to sign Inter Milan captain Lautaro Martinez as Julian Alvarez and Victor Osimhen alternative’
Sports.content:
ARSENAL reportedly made a play for Lautaro Martinez after realising they wouldn’t be able to land Julian Alvarez.

The Gunners were hopeful of convincing the wantaway Atletico Madrid ace to join them this summer in a blockbuster transfer.



But the former Manchester City striker ended up staying in the Spanish capital, where he faces an uncertain future.

And it’s claimed that Gunners boss Mikel Arteta, who was also linked with a swoop for Galatasaray‘s Victor Osimhen, explored the possibility of bringing Martinez to the Emirates after it became clear Alvarez would be going nowhere.



That’s according to The Daily Mail, who claim Gunners assistant coach Gabriel Heinze reached out to his fellow Argentine to gauge his interest in coming to the Premier League.

The north Londoners’ reported aspirations of a late swoop for Martinez are said to have been emphatically shot down by Italian champions Inter Milan.

Arsenal would’ve been hard-pressed to convince the striker, who broke England fans’ hearts in the World Cup semi-final, to jump ship as he’d previously snubbed a potential move to Barcelona.

In May, he said of his future: “No doubt I would like to retire at this club.

“It’s hard for me to imagine myself anywhere else these days.

“You never know in football but if they don’t kick me out, I’m staying here.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

When pressed on Barca’s pursuit of his services, Martinez told Sky Italia: “The rumours were true.

“But in the end, I wanted to stay here with my teammates, with these people, with these fans who have always been magnificent to me.

“It’s definitely a great pleasure, a great honour, and a huge satisfaction because you’re always working to improve, to move forward, to become better.



“When these offers or calls from these huge clubs arrive, they’re always welcome. It’s a very important thing.

“Now I’m in a city that has supported me incredibly since day one.

“I have a restaurant, my kids go to school. I’ll always be here because I feel good, because I’m happy.

Arsenal will be back in action on Sunday afternoon, welcoming big-spending Chelsea to the Emirates.

Martinez and his Inter team-mates, meanwhile, will face Napoli at the San Siro on Saturday evening.

Sports.title: Ollie Watkins’ wife Ellie chokes up as she bids Aston Villa farewell before England star scores on Al-Hilal debut
Sports.content:
OLLIE WATKINS’ wife Ellie fought back tears as she issued an emotional farewell to Aston Villa after moving to Saudi Arabia.

Watkins, 30, moved to Al-Hilal after six glittering years at Villa that saw him registering 108 goals and 47 assists in 278 appearances that included Champions League outings and a Europa League triumph.



The striker’s exit from Villa Park included a short period of acrimony as he refused to play in the Premier League opener at Brighton that saw Unai Emery’s side getting thrashed 4-0 in a disastrous start .

But the England international returned to apologise to Villa manager Emery before his switch to the Middle East was confirmed and later issued a touching farewell video to the fans.



Ellie, 30, followed suit after she, her husband and their children Amara, 4, and Marley, 3 arrived in Riyadh.

The content creator shared a clip on TikTok where she choked up as she discussed how hard it’s been leaving their lives in the UK.

Ellie said: “Okay, well that wasn’t on my bingo card for 2026.

“We are in Riyadh, we arrived in Saudi last night and I think I’m still in shock to be honest like how life can change so quickly but that is the joys of football.

“I’ve always actually said how lucky I think we are because we’ve been at Villa for six years which in football terms is actually quite a long time.

“We’ve had our children there, we’ve had quite big life events so it feels bittersweet to me. I loved my life there, I settled so well and made the most amazing friends.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“So I am feeling quite emotional about leaving that behind. But I am excited for a change of scenery, I think it’s going to be amazing for the kids and I think they are going to have the best time ever.

“Once we are settled and we know what we are doing, it will all be good. Getting on with our new life in Saudi, so exciting times.

“I’m also feeling a little nervous but I remember feeling like that when we moved to Birmingham so hopefully you can follow my journey in Saudi.”

Watkins enjoyed a glittering start to life at Al-Hilal as he scored on his debut on Tuesday that led to a 3-0 victory over Al-Ahli.



The centre-forward has linked up with a number of notable names, such as Kalidou Koulibaly, Theo Hernandez, Yassine Bounou, Ruben Neves, Sergej Milinkovic-Savic and Crysencio Summerville.

They are also expected to be joined by Gabriel Martinelli, who is heading out of Arsenal.

Sports.title: Man Utd fans call for Jason Wilcox to QUIT after Red Devils failed to sign new left back in poor end to transfer window
Sports.content:
DISGRUNTLED Manchester United fans have called for Jason Wilcox to RESIGN after the club’s underwhelming transfer window.

The Red Devils revamped their midfield by bringing in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba for a combined £149million.



However, issues in defence and attack, including the need for a new striker and a very pressing need for a new left-back, failed to be addressed by club transfer chiefs.

Fans were left disappointed with this reality in a window where many felt more was needed to cope with the rigours of also playing Champions League football.



SunSport’s Man Utd correspondent Samuel Luckhurst rated the window as a 6/10, arguing this term “could be a season of consolidation” in maintaining a place in the top four, rather than a title challenge.

But Man Utd technical director Jason Wilcox has been called out online.

Meanwhile, sensational reports have also claimed the club’s director of recruitment Christopher Vivell could also be on his way out.

Such a suggestion sparked an increase in ire from sections of the fanbase, with one saying: “We’re all wearing this same face after seeing this transfer market. #Berradaout. #WilcoxOut.”

A second said: “I don’t care what happens anymore. This clown (Wilcox) needs to be sacked. NOW!!!”

A third added: “Vivell will 100 per cent leave. He can’t work with the absolute clowns he is surrounded by. Why is it never the dummies that leave?!”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Another said: “Sack the f***ing lot of them, clown show FC.”

A fifth fumed: “Don’t fall for it either… Net spend of £85m this summer and they want you to believe they will spend £500m next year? Disgusting c***s they really are. Every bit of failure is on Ineos this season.”

Bayern Munich were linked with Vivell last month as they seek a replacement for chief scout Nils Schmadtke, who could be on his way out of the Bavarian club.

Though Bayern chief Max Eberl played down those rumours, at least for the time being, as he said: “Nils has one year left on his contract, just like I do.

“We shouldn’t be defaming people. That’s a touch too much for me right now.”



Vivell, 39, joined Man Utd in 2024 – the same year as Wilcox – having previously been the technical director at Chelsea between 2022 and 2023.

The German was also the technical director at RB Leipzig between 2020 and 2022, and was a scout for the Bundesliga side for five years before that, having started scouting at Hoffenheim in 2010.

Man Utd beat Ipswich 5-2 at Old Trafford last weekend but lost away to Hull in their opening game of the season.

They visit Everton next before hosting Azerbaijani side, Sabah, in the Champions League, followed by the Manchester City, also at home.

Sports.title: Chelsea and Tottenham leave Arsenal and Man Utd in their wake as winners and losers of summer transfer window revealed
Sports.content:
IT was the maddest, biggest, most astonishing summer transfer window of all time.

Record-breaking sums and huge squad overhauls, with the drama extending to two hours after the deadline as Everton’s big striker signing changed his mind after the last minute.



As the dust settles, the debates on who were the Prem winners and losers will intensify.

SunSport sifts through the chaos to identify those with something to smile about. And those left with scowls.



WINNERS

Chelsea:

Even by Stamford Bridge standards, this has been a stunning summer of shifting sands.

But while midfield depth may be an issue – given the injury records of Moises Caicedo, Romeo Lavia and Reece James and the collapse of the deal for Monaco’s Lamine Camara – new boss Xabi Alonso seems to have all his other ducks in a row.



Morgan Rogers’ £117m arrival has already paid off alongside Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer, Maxence Lacroix is utterly at home at centre-halves, while Blues fans like the look of full-backs Marco Palestra and Pep Chavarria.

Even the signing Chelsea did not want to make, before Robert Sanchez’ failings made the move for Emi Martinez a no-brainer, has boosted the squad.

Hull:

The Tigers had two options after their unexpected promotion.

They could have taken the easy way out, spent a few bob, accepted their fate, used the guaranteed £220m over the next three years to give them a platform to come back stronger.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Instead, it’s a copy of the playbook that saw Sunderland exceed all expectations last summer – and then some.

In total, 18 new players and the third-highest net spend in the Prem. They even let the bloke who scored their winner at Coventry on Saturday go out on loan on deadline day. Full marks for ambition.

Liverpool:

Bradley Barcola’s £123m arrival was the landmark deal of the Anfield summer – but Andoni Iraola putting his foot down to keep Cody Gakpo might be equally important.

Spaniard Victor Munoz has already made a good impression, winning the penalty that earned a point at Newcastle on the opening weekend before scoring the leveller against Forest on Saturday.

Young Frenchman Jeremy Jacquet could be the partner to keep Virgil van Dijk fresh for the fight at the back, while there are doubts about both full-backs.



Yet if Alexander Isak can profit from the men on either flank, Liverpool could be back in the title mix.

Manchester City:

Life after Pep was always going to be different, yet few could have imagined quite how different.

Overhauling the entire midfield – at a cost of just £327m – was a signal of City’s laser focus on giving Enzo Maresca the chance to get off to a trophy-winning start.

But while City have lost the experience of Rodri, they look to have plenty of goals in them – as long as Erling Haaland stays fit.



Enzo Fernandez will add midfield goals, Iliman Ndiaye something different to the mix, while Rayan Cherki already looks in the mood to make this a launchpad season.

Tottenham:

Well, they should be, anyway, after an unprecedented summer splurge in North London.

This is “Roberto De Zerbi’s Tottenham”, in every sense, all 10 new recruits bearing the manager’s mark.

Now the onus is on the Italian manager to turn the ingredients he put in the pot into something tasty – although there has been a distinct lack of seasoning so far.

Spurs fans have reason to be demanding and that will put pressure on Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Savio and Omar Marmoush in particular.



De Zerbi must make sure they aren’t “N17th” again.

LOSERS

Arsenal:

The expectation was that the champions would improve from a position of strength.

Instead, while Ezri Konsa and Bruno Guimaraes add to the previous strong points of Mikel Arteta’s side, his forward options look weaker.

For all the efforts to land Vinicius Jr, Arsenal look like they were played by the Brazilian and his representatives, leaving Greek winger Christos Solis as the only attacking reinforcement.

Meanwhile, Arsenal allowed Gabriel Jesus, Leandro Trossard and Reiss Nelson to leave, with Gabriel Martinelli Saudi-bound as well.



Fans are asking big questions of sporting director Andrea Berta. It is hard to argue Arteta has a better squad than he ended last term with.

Aston Villa:

It might look very different in May but for now Unai Emery appears to have been asked to undertake a massive job in building almost an entirely new side from scratch.

Losing six of the 11 players who started the Europa League final feels like a seismic change, even if Emery loves a challenge.

Villa have been slow starters in the past, only to pick up the pace quickly and end up as a potent force in both the Prem and Europe.

This time, though, they need all the new recruits to get up to speed quickly, in the most competitive league in the world.

Crystal Palace:

You’ve got to feel sorry for Pierre Sage, whose spirits are unlikely to be lifted by parsley, rosemary or thyme.

The new Palace boss inherited a side that had lost two of its three star assets last term, with Eberechi Eze leaving for Arsenal and Marc Guehi at Manchester City.

While he did keep Adam Wharton – surely a January target for someone – Sage saw wing-back Daniel Munoz join predecessor Oliver Glasner at Forest and Lacroix’s switch to Chelsea, while Jean-Philippe Mateta unsuccessfully asked Fifa to rip up his contract and Ismaila Sarr is in a right old huff.

Even the Holmesdale Massive are hacked off. Nobody looks to be “glad all over” at Selhurst.



Everton:

The joke was biting, but fair.

Everton – the only team with more stadiums than strikers. And left-backs. And right-backs.

Over the space of three days, the Toffees moved for Richarlison, Joshua Zirkzee, and Folarin Balogun but were rejected by all of them.

And while few Evertonians will mourn the departure of Beto, selling Iliman Ndiaye to take a punt on Jack Grealish’s second loan spell is hardly a bet you’d put more than a fiver on.

Fans are in uproar – even after making the club backtrack over the proposed sale of Harrison Armstrong – and the mood is beyond dark.



You wonder how much longer David Moyes will put up with being ordered to fight with both hands tied behind his back?

Manchester United:

Yes, a new-look midfield – although Carlos Baleba is still injured and Andrey Santos was dropped after one game.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But other than that, United are pretty much exactly the same as they were, which has left Old Trafford fans wondering what the club is playing at.

Deadline day efforts to find a back-up – or replacement – for Luke Shaw were too little and too late, Diogo Dalot is hardly the ideal choice on the right, while they looked vulnerable to pace through the middle even while beating Ipswich on Sunday.

Sports.title: Tottenham misfit Richarlison lined up for sensational Mo Salah strike partnership as Trabzonspor target late transfer
Sports.content:
TOTTENHAM striker Richarlison has emerged as a shock target for Turkish side Trabzonspor.

The Brazilian has been left in limbo after turning down the chance to join Everton before Tuesday’s transfer deadline.

Richarlison hinted he wanted to stay at Spurs via a bombshell statement that said “no one will ever again decide my future”.



But Tottenham are now braced for a formal approach from Trabzonspor, who want to sign a striker this week.



The Turkish transfer window does not close until on Friday and West Ham striker Pablo is another player on their radar.

Richarlison is thought to be open to the idea of moving to Trabzonspor, but agreeing a fee with Spurs may prove tricky.

Tottenham were set to bank £35million by selling the Brazil forward to Everton before the deal collapsed.



Trabzonspor would be able to offer hefty wages, as shown by the contract that Salah penned with them.

The Egyptian signed a two-year deal in August that is worth £363,000 a week – AFTER TAX.

Club president Ertugrul Dogan was behind Trabzonspor’s push to sign Salah and is expected to play a leading role in the pitch to Richarlison.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

If Richarlison were to depart, he’d join Luka Vuskovic, Cristian Romero and Djed Spence among the big name departures.



Should he remain, he has a fight on his hands to find a role in the team with Spurs signing Savio, Omar Marmoush and Mykhalo Mudryk in attacking positions.

Sports.title: Chelsea transfer window ranked as Xabi Alonso strikes gold with Morgan Rogers but could be left short in key area
Sports.content:
CHELSEA fans were one decision away from a seemingly perfect transfer window.

And that decision was not one of their own but one made by AS Monaco, after pulling out of a deal for midfielder Lamine Camara at the final hour, who was supposed to replace Enzo Fernandez.



Still, the Blues’ first window with Xabi Alonso at the helm is something to be marveled at in terms of incomings, but especially in terms of outgoings.

The signing of Morgan Rogers looks to have given them one of the most dangerous forward lines in the Premier League, with Maxence Lacroix enforcing their defence, and Emiliano Martinez replacing the inconsistent Robert Sanchez in goal.



Those three were joined by the incomings of Marco Palestra, Danny Welbeck, Jordan Henderson, Pep Chavarria, Valentin Barco, Honest Anahor, Geovany Quenda, and Dastan Satpayev.

If they had have replaced the outgoing Fernandez with Camara they would total 12 new players who all bring vastly different qualities.

MORGAN ROGERS – 9

£117m from Aston Villa

Rogers’ signing from Aston Villa has started very brightly, and got everyone talking about Chelsea‘s ‘JP Morgan’ or ‘CPR’ front three.

He has a great relationship with Cole Palmer, who also seems to be back on track and boosted by Rogers’ signing, and has scored and assisted in the Prem already.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

It’s a hefty fee, which makes him the most expensive English player of all time, but so far he looks to be proving his worth.

So far, signing him looks a very smart move from The Blues, and one that could even propel them to the title if things work out.



EMILIANO MARTINEZ – 8

£7.5m from Aston Villa

For such a cheap fee, it’s hard to argue that this will be a bad signing for Chelsea.

Robert Sanchez was incredibly error prone, and Martinez is a proven top-level goalkeeper who has won numerous trophies and individual awards, as well as being a leader and adding experience to the side.

However, he is just as, if not more mistake-prone than Sanchez – and it will be a waiting game to see how much that impacts Chelsea and the value of his signing.

MAXENCE LACROIX – 8

£52m from Crystal Palace

Perhaps a little pricey, but undoubtedly what Chelsea needed at the back.



A Premier League proven defender who is comfortable in a back three system, with recovery pace to burn and of a good age profile for what this Chelsea team need.

The Frenchman has been exceptional so far, and especially strong against Fulham where he bagged an assist.

Admittedly, the Blues defence still looks particularly shaky even with him in it, but the missing Moises Caicedo won’t be helping that one bit.

MARCO PALESTRA – 7

£43m from Bologna

The Italian wingback has already been dubbed the ‘next Marcos Alonso‘ at Stamford Bridge.



Problem with that being, he was great going forward, but had obvious shortcomings in defence – something Palestra seems to share with him,

For £43m, the upside to his signing certainly outweights the potential downside, and he looks a promising signing from pre-season despite picking up an injury that has seen him miss the opening two matches of the Premier League.

DANNY WELBECK – 7

£5m from Brighton

What Welbeck brings to this team is obvious, experience and goals.

He will be a good, much-needed leader for Alonso, and has already bagged his first goal in blue in the Carabao Cup.



JORDAN HENDERSON – 7

Free from Brentford

The midfielder is yet to really do anything since joining Chelsea, given his overhanging injury from the World Cup.

That said, he has been taking up something of a coaching role under Alonso and will have a good impact on the dressing room.

Having signed on a free it’s hard to give him a bad mark, and he might even get some minutes in the absence of Fernandez.

VALENTIN BARCO – 8

£33.6m from Strasbourg

Wasn’t given much of a chance by fans when he first signed, but actually already looks a very astute signing.

He’s versatile, and can play as a full-back or a midfielder, shining in the Carabao Cup arguably more than any other player – dubbed a mix of Kevin De Bruyne and N’Golo Kante.



If he turns out to be anywhere near as good as either of those, he will be a success.

PEP CHAVARRIA – 7

£16.3m from Rayo Vallecano

Compared mostly to Cesar Azpilicueta, Chavarria has been solid when he has played for Chelsea so far.

He seems like largely a backup option on the left to the likes of Jorrel Hato and Marco Palestra, but a solid one nonetheless when he has played, and again is the right age profile for what Chelsea needed in this window.

GEOVANY QUENDA – 7

£44m from Sporting

A very, very exciting winger who can also play wingback under Xabi Alonso.



He is versatile and looks fresh in the same way Estevao did when he was breaking onto the scene at Stamford Bridge last season.

When he has played he looks direct and willing to take on his man, and you would imagine he is someone that if Chelsea do ever need to offload that they will profit on.

DASTAN SATPAYEV – 8

£3.5m from Kairat Almaty

Is spending the season on loan at Burnley, but it’s hard to imagine the Blues’ ‘baby Aguero’ not at least turning them a profit in the future.

He has also looked promising when he has actually played under Alonso, scoring a goal in pre-season.



HONEST ANAHOR – ?

£40m from Atalanta

Is supposedly the next best defender to come out of Serie A, and will spend this season at Crystal Palace before joining Chelsea in 2027.

£40m is a lot of money for a centre-back who will need to impress at Palace this season.

OVERALL RATING: 8/10

Xabi Alonso has been given the ‘manager’ title at Stamford Bridge, and it shows.

He has addressed almost every problem area in the squad, apart from the central midfield position where the late departure of Enzo Fernandez has left a hole.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

A new goalkeeper in Emi Martinez and the additions of Maxence Lacroix and Morgan Rogers address issues from qualitative depth to a lack of experience from last season, and seem to suit Alonso’s system nicely.

Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson should provide experience and squad depth, while Chelsea have also sold brilliantly and still brought promising youth in the form of Anahor, Quenda and Satpayev, who will likely make them a profit or become superstars themselves.

Sports.title: Why Man Utd struggle to sell players – one legend departed for ‘peanuts’ and serial winners have left for cut-price fees
Sports.content:
THIRTY-ONE years ago, Manchester United sold three first-teamers and did not make a single signing.

If social media existed in the summer of 1995, the internet might have crashed. Paul Ince, Andrei Kanchelskis and Mark Hughes, integral to Alex Ferguson’s first great side, each had a unique bond with the fanbase.



United banked £14million for the trio, an enormous sum three years after the Premier League’s inception. They have not had many summers like it since.

Ideally, United would have jettisoned a midfielder, a winger and a forward this summer, too. Manuel Ugarte, Marcus Rashford and Joshua Zirkzee were unshiftable.



For a club that received a world record fee for Cristiano Ronaldo in 2009, United are historically bad sellers.

They gave David Beckham away for “peanuts” to Real Madrid at the height of the Galactico era. Anthony Martial, Paul Pogba and Jadon Sancho signed for deals worth a combined £219.9m within a six-year period and were released.



There is no short answer to why United are bad at selling. You could write a hefty tome or record a podcast series on their poor record and why they struggle to fetch fees for senior players.

It was not even 18 months ago that United suffered their worst season in 51 years. So their current squad is not teeming with sellable assets and hardly anyone is capable of raking in a profit.

Altay Bayindir, loaned to Celta Vigo, is renowned for letting in goals. Joshua Zirkzee, the subject of a desperate loan enquiry from Everton on Tuesday evening, is renowned for not scoring goals.

Of all Everton’s window missteps, selling Beto and moving for Zirkzee should spark sackings. Beto scored five times as many goals as Zirkzee last season.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The extravagant salaries United have put players on made them no-goes. Marcus Rashford is only still at the club as no elite European side was prepared to foot his wage bill of £325,000-a-week.

Casemiro saw out his contract as he was immovable. United are bound to encounter the same issue with Mason Mount, into the final two years of his deal and on £250,000 a week.

Jaap Stam, Cristiano Ronaldo, Daley Blind, Chris Smalling and Daniel James would be an obscure five-a-side team. They are also the only players United bought and sold at an eight-figure profit.

Ronaldo, James, Beckham, Angel di Maria, Romelu Lukaku, Scott McTominay, Mason Greenwood, Alejandro Garnacho and Rasmus Hojlund are the only United players to leave for £25m or more.

Of those nine players, four came through the club’s academy. That was the only source of United’s transfer income negotiated this summer, via Toby Collyer and Radek Vitek.



Garnacho, valued north of £85m in 2024, left for £40m in 2025. The most senior sale in the window that just closed was Collyer, starter of three games against Barnsley, Rangers and Steaua Bucharest. The last of those was in January 2025.

United trumpeted the overall £7.6m fee West Brom agreed to pay, with £3m up front. A source said it is “unlikely” the add-ons will be triggered.

The academy sells as United have produced talented professionals for the best part of a century. Andreas Pereira (£10m), James Garner (£15m), Dean Henderson (£20m), Anthony Elanga (£15m) and Garnacho all moved to Premier League clubs before Collyer and Vitek dropped down to the Championship.



In the summer of 2022, United’s only sales were Pereira and Garner. They had been out on loan, so were not damaged by the cataclysmic season with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and then Ralf Rangnick in the dugout.

Although Ferguson rarely drove a hard bargain, he did not struggle for willing takers. In 2007, Ferguson’s friend Sam Allardyce, had just been installed at Newcastle, who signed Alan Smith for £6m

Roy Keane could barely stomach sharing the same oxygen as Ferguson after United sacked him but still signed five players from his former club during his two-and-a-half years as Sunderland manager.

Steve Bruce, also at Sunderland, gave Wes Brown and John O’Shea a new home in 2011. David Moyes was a sucker for a United reject at Everton.

There were no domestic or Uefa financial rules to comply with back then, either. That was largely the case when Ed Woodward regularly misread a player’s market value.



The die was cast in the summer of 2014. New manager Louis van Gaal was decisive in identifying which players’ faces did not fit, so Woodward sanctioned several sales with little or no negotiating.

Shinji Kagawa left for roughly half the price United paid for him in 2012. Michael Keane and Wilfried Zaha were both flogged for £3m with no sell-on clauses inserted. £16m for Danny Welbeck was, in hindsight, low.

The squad purge continued in Van Gaal’s second summer: £4.25m for Nani, £6m for Jonny Evans and £7.3m for Javier Hernandez. Serial winners sold at a cut price amid mismanagement.



So a precedent was set: United sold on the cheap. Keane moved from Burnley to Everton for £30m in 2017. West Ham bought Hernandez in the same summer for more than double the £7.3m Bayer Leverkusen paid United. Evans was wanted by Manchester City at one stage.

Morgan Schneiderlin (£24m) and Memphis Depay (£21m) left for impressive fees in January 2017. The difference then was United were a resurgent force under Jose Mourinho and the players were cut loose after 18 months, so had suffered little reputational damage.

United banked good fees for Blind (£18.5m) and Sam Johnstone (£10m) in July 2018. Their reputations were enhanced by association with Mourinho and, in Johnstone’s case, emerging from the United academy.

But United regressed in the seller’s market after finishing sixth in 2018-19. Ander Herrera ran down his contract and Lukaku was sold at a minor loss to Inter Milan.



United had a decent 2024 as the majority of their outgoings were academy talents as part of Ineos’s attempts to use it as a cash cow.

There was an obvious market for Aaron Wan-Bissaka, a right back with six-and-a-half years of Premier League experience.

Coming 15th and trophyless in 2025 demanded outgoings. Ruben Amorim’s ‘bomb squad’ made certain players’ positions untenable, though United sold Antony at a considerable loss and failed to obtain a higher fee for Garnacho.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

There was never going to be a fire sale this summer and Michael Carrick’s nature meant anyone ‘for sale’ had a squad role if they stayed.



Ugarte is no Ince and Zirkzee is no Hughes. Rashford has trumped Kanchelskis, though.

Sports.title: Inside Enzo Fernandez’s love life, from brief split with childhood sweetheart to Wanda Nara slipping into his DM’s
Sports.content:
ENZO FERNANDEZ has joined Man City in a joint British record transfer.

The Argentine midfielder, 25, swapped Stamford Bridge for the Etihad on transfer deadline day for £125million.



The move will see Enzo uprooting his family, from London to Manchester, as he settles in to his new club.

Away from the pitch, the World Cup winner is in a longterm relationship with stunning influencer, Valentina Cervantes.



The high school sweethearts share two children, Olivia and Benjamin.

However, there was trouble in paradise when Enzo and Valentina briefly split in late 2024.



They reconciled in 2025, but then he found himself in an alleged love triangle with Wanda Nara.

And Valentina was also said to be charmed by an unnamed Argentina international.

Enzo’s love life has certainly been complicated in the last few years.

Young love

Valentina and Enzo met in 2018 and soon became love struck teenagers in Buenos Aires.



She said: “I met Enzo when he was 16, and at 17 we moved in together. We’re both from San Martín, we have a group of friends in common.

“He used to go on vacation to Mar del Tuyú, and in 2018 I went there with my family, and that’s when I really got to know him.

“We’d see each other on the beach, we talked that summer, and it wasn’t until the end of the year that we actually got together. For our first date, he invited me to the nephew’s country house, which was for his birthday.”



Olivia, their first born, arrived in 2020, and they soon became young parents.

She revealed: “When Olivia was born, we were living in a studio apartment in Urquiza, which Enzo’s agent paid for.

“During the pandemic, the three of us were there, and I was working at a call centre, while he didn’t have a salary yet. At that time, we bought our daughter’s used clothes on Facebook Marketplace.

“We used to take the bus; Enzo would get off at General Paz and catch another one to River, and I’d keep going to the Urquiza station because I worked downtown at an empanada shop, and later at the call centre near the Obelisk.”

In 2022, Enzo moved from River Plate to Benfica. Valentina and Olivia uprooted to Lisbon to start a new life.



But, they weren’t there long. Some five months after he made his debut for the Portuguese giants, Enzo was transferred again.

This time, it was Chelsea calling in a then British record £107million deal.

Valentina and Olivia followed once more, before they could catch their breath in Portugal.

In October 2023, Enzo and Valentina welcomed a son to their brood, when Benjamin was born.



On the surface, they seemed to be the happiest of families. But, underneath the surface, cracks were beginning to show.

A brief split

In November 2024, Enzo and Valentina had parted ways.

Argentine journalist Julieta Argenta claimed that Fernandez told her he wanted to “live alone”.

She added context in a social media post, writing: “They’re still family, but he feels the need to experience the stage he skipped by choosing family early on.”



Valentina admitted she was blindsided by the break-up in an interview with Paparazzi magazine.

She said: “Everything was fine and suddenly one day he told me that he didn’t want to be anymore. There are things that I still have to process, but that’s it, I accepted it.”

Valentina confessed that she cried for five minutes when Fernandez told her about the breakup, but her background of being the daughter of separated parents shaped her perspective.



It got complicated

Barely three months after they went their separate ways, Enzo seemingly had a change of heart.

They were seen walking around London kissing and holding hands, and it seemed their romance was back on

But, reports in Argentina claimed that he moved to repair his relationship, after finding out an unnamed Argentina international team-mate had tried to seduce Valentina.

In an explosive claim about the midfielder’s apparent decision to backtrack on his decision, journalist Daniel Fava revealed it was linked to a move by another member of Argentina’s winning World Cup squad on Enzo’s long-time partner.

Fava said on TV show A la tarde in January 2025: “In the last few hours there’s been a reconciliation with his ex-partner Valentina Cervantes. They’re giving things another go.”



He added: “The information I have is that Enzo Fernandez is desperately trying to win her back because he’s heard that a fellow world champion is sniffing around her.”

The Argentine journalist offered no further clues about the identity of the mystery player he was pointing the finger at, or whether he even knew his name.



After a colleague interrupted to say: “What you’re saying is that he prefers to get back with her than see another man jumping in,” he said of Valentina: “Today she’s prettier than ever.

“Since the separation she has gained a new sex appeal and energy” before making a second bombshell claim “more than one footballer” had contacted her over social media since the shock split.

A fly in the ointment

Not long after Enzo and Valentina had rekindled their romance, it was claimed that blonde beauty Wanda Nara had slipped into his DM’s.

Wanda hosts Celebrity Masterchef in her homeland, and back in October 2025 Valentina was a contestant on the show.

Reports in Argentina said Wanda and Valentina appeared frosty with each other, and apparently for good reason too.



According to La Nacion, Wanda sent Enzo a flirty message that read: “I just saw you around the neighbourhood, write to me if you want.”

It’s claimed that, rather than respond, he immediately showed the message to Valentina.

And this is allegedly what annoyed Wanda.



Valentina blasted reports of alleged messages between her man and Wanda.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She said: “Yes, I saw it. No, as far as I know, I haven’t seen any messages.

“No, no, Enzo never spoke to me about anything. No, he never spoke to me about any of that.”

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Man Utd deal announced, Arsenal double move, Folarin Balogun bombshell
Sports.content:
Latest transfer news from Manchester United, Arsenal, Liverpool and more - as Premier League clubs break summer window record with £3.2billion spend

After a major summer of spending, the Premier League's summer transfer window drew to a close at 11pm on Tuesday evening. It was a record-shattering couple of months across the UK, with a total exceeding £3.2billion exceeded through deals.

Manchester City and Chelsea agreed a £125m deal for Enzo Fernandez, with the wantaway midfielder finally leaving Stamford Bridge after months of speculation regarding his future. The Cityzens also welcomed Iliman Ndiaye to their ranks in a £65m move, further bolstering Enzo Maresca's choice.

Sunderland's approach of Malick Fofana also dominated the headlines on Tuesday, with what should have been a straightforward move turning into quite the saga when Crystal Palace threatened to hijack the Black Cats' move.

With Kyril Louis-Dreyfus flying to Lyon to persuade the 21-year-old winger to join his project at the Stadium of Light, Fofana gave Sunderland the green-light to put the wheels in motion on a move, forced to submit a dealsheet to ensure a transfer due to the last-minute nature of his decision.

In West London, AS Monaco also knocked back Chelsea's £47m move for Lamine Camara in dramatic fashion. Everything had been agreed between the two clubs, when Monaco pulled the plug with just minutes to go until the deadline - with Everton's endeavours of securing Folarin Balogun having a knock-on effect.

Chelsea were reportedly left fuming with the incredibly unprofessional last-minute decision. And Balogun's deal didn't go through anyway, with Monaco's sporting director sensationally claiming it was the striker who walked away from the deal after 'feeling mistreated' during his medical.

Mykhailo Mudryk also joined Tottenham Hotspur on a season-long loan, with both clubs hopeful that the Ukrainian is able to reacclimate to the pace of the Premier League after a two-year lay-off.

Sports.title: Liverpool considered 8 wingers in summer transfer window before landing Bradley Barcola
Sports.content:
Liverpool considered 8 wingers in summer transfer window before landing Bradley Barcola

Liverpool made Bradley Barcola their final signing of the summer after sealing a £123million deal with Paris Saint-Germain but the Reds had a number of alternatives to the French winger

View 2 Images Liverpool eventually sealed a deal for Bradley Barcola (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool had as many as eight alternatives to Bradley Barcola in the summer transfer window, including England’s Anthony Gordon and Real Madrid star Endrick.

‌



The Reds came into the window needing additions out wide following Mohamed Salah’s exit. They eventually signed Barcola in a £123million deal after a summer-long search followed by drawn-out negotiations with former side Paris Saint-Germain.

‌



But it is well known that the Frenchman was not the only player that Liverpool chiefs had in mind. Former RB Leipzig star Yan Diomande was a high-profile target, albeit Real Madrid swooped in to seal his services instead.

‌



And that appears to have been the theme with a host of their potential attacking targets. Former Everton and Newcastle man Anthony Gordon was an early possibility but he instead moved to Barcelona for £69m after the Spanish side chose not to activate their permanent £26m option for Manchester United’s Marcus Rashford.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Liverpool were also left frustrated as their attempts to sign Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh ended without a positive result. Brighton received bids of £50m and £60m for the Gambian but chose to turn them down.

While Minteh eventually stayed where he was, the same cannot be said of the rest of Liverpool’s shortlist. Matias Fernandez-Pardo had emerged as an option following his standout performances for French side Lille, with Newcastle sealing a late deal worth £51m for his services.

Lyon wideman Malick Fofana was also eyed by Liverpool, but he too opted for a move to the north east, having sealed a deadline day switch to Sunderland.

‌



View 2 Images Liverpool were previously interested in Anthony Gordon (Image: Getty Images)

Away from Barcola, Liverpool also had another PSG winger in mind in their search for attacking reinforcements. Ibrahim Mbaye was eventually on the move to the Premier League but signed for Aston Villa.

Their final two options were Real Madrid’s Endrick and Koln’s Said El Mala, but they eventually stayed with their current clubs.

‌



That left Liverpool pursuing a deal for Barcola, who is keen to lift silverware at Anfield. He said: "I hope to achieve very big thingsFirst of all, winning the Premier League – it's one of my biggest dreams in my life.

"It is to do that and to stay in this team in the long term – that's why I signed a long contract – and I hope I can do it.

"It's a great pride to be able to play for Liverpool. I'm very happy. It took a long time but I'm really happy to be able to play for Liverpool and all I want is to be on the pitch and be able to play."

Sports.title: Scott McTominay breaks silence on his upcoming heart surgery after Napoli statement
Sports.content:
Scott McTominay breaks silence on his upcoming heart surgery after Napoli statement

Scott McTominay has offered some clarity after Napoli announced that the Scotland international will undergo heart surgery on "a mild benign arrhythmia" in the coming days

View 2 Images Scott McTominay has explained his surgery (Image: Pier Marco Tacca/Getty Images)

Scott McTominay has reassured Napoli and Scotland fans that he is "fine" after Napoli announced he would undergo heart surgery.

‌



The Italian club released a statement on Tuesday explaining the situation. It read: "Following the onset of a mild benign arrhythmia, Scott McTominay will undergo corrective surgery using a cardiac arrhythmia ablation (PFA) in the coming days. He will be available again after the international break."

‌



While the announcement about his arrhythmia - an irregular heartbeat - came as a shock to many supporters, McTominay says it is nothing serious. “I’m fine, the procedure was something I’d planned to do with the club for quite a while,” he told reporters at the Gran Gala Del Calcio, the Italian equivalent of the PFA Awards, on Wednesday night.

‌



“We’d already talked about it in pre-season. I’ll be out for a few weeks.”

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

McTominay is a key player for Napoli, having joined the club from Manchester United for £25million in 2024. He has scored 27 goals in 82 games for Napoli and helped them win Serie A in 2024/25.

‌



He was named Serie A player of the year for 2025 for his incredible debut campaign and will be important to their efforts to reclaim the trophy following Inter Milan's triumph last season.

The 29-year-old midfielder has started both of Napoli's matches this season but is now set for a short spell on the sidelines. While he still has two years left on his contract, there has been some speculation in Italy over his future.

View 2 Images Scott McTominay is set for a spell on the sidelines (Image: Insidefoto, Insidefoto/LightRocket via Getty Images)

‌



“There haven’t been any new talks,” McTominay said when asked about a possible extension. “The important thing is what happens on the pitch, not the contract extension. I don’t know when it will happen, it’s not the time to be thinking about that.”

Napoli began the campaign with a 2-0 win over Genoa before losing 2-1 to Cesc Fabregas' Como on the weekend. Fellow former Manchester United player Rasmus Hojlund netted the consolation against Como, while ex-Manchester City star Kevin De Bruyne scored on the opening weekend.

Max Allegri is now the man in charge at Napoli and he explained after the Como defeat that McTominay was also dealing with a different kind of health issue.

‌



“McTominay had some problems with blisters, so he’s been training on a limited basis," Allegri said. "Hopefully, we can get him into the best possible condition as soon as possible.”

The Scottish star will sit out of the next four Napoli games and will be a big miss. Napoli take on Inter Milan on Saturday, ahead of a Champions League clash with Premier League champions Arsenal and further league games against Bologna and Fiorentina.

Sports.title: Jadon Sancho career lifeline emerges as ex-Man Utd ace eyed for free agent offer
Sports.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Jadon Sancho career lifeline emerges as ex-Man Utd ace eyed for free agent offer

EXCLUSIVE: Jadon Sancho was left without a club this summer, but a lifeline for the former Manchester United ace could soon present itself

View 3 Images Jadon Sancho is currently without a club (Image: 2026 UEFA)

Ambitious Dubai side Arabian Falcons are preparing a pitch for former Manchester United star and free agent Jadon Sancho to join them.

‌



The Falcons are managed by ex-Liverpool and England ace Jonjo Shelvey, and have Leicester City Premier League winner Danny Simpson as a player-coach. When the transfer window slammed shut, Sancho was left without a club having been released by United at the end of June.

‌



Aston Villa opted not to make his loan move permanent, after signing him temporarily last season. It means Sancho is currently stuck in the wilderness of free agency, five years after signing for United from Borussia Dortmund for £72.9m.

‌



Fast forward to the present day, the Falcons are preparing to reach out to Sancho and other big name free agents without a club.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Mirror Football understands the Emirati football club are plotting an ambitious pitch to sway the likes of Sancho towards the club. They have already convinced one former United prodigy Ravel Morrison, who signed last summer and was recently made the captain of the side, to move to the Middle East.

‌



Sancho was linked with moves to Fiorentina and Roma, although neither club opted to sign him. He has also been linked with a surprise move to Brazilian side Palmeiras.

The former England international, who scored three goals in 23 international caps for the Three Lions, has played for four clubs in the last three seasons, including the appearances he made for United in the 2023-24 campaign

View 3 Images Shelvey is now in charge of Arabian Falcons (Image: Arabian Falcons FC)

‌



He had an emotional return to Dortmund on loan in the 2024 January transfer window and even played in the Champions League final at Wembley Stadium, which the German heavyweights lost 2-0 to Real Madrid.

After Dortmund opted not to sign him permanently, he spent a season on loan at Chelsea, where he won the Europa Conference League. A permanent move to Stamford Bridge not only didn't transpire, the Blues paid a £5m penalty fee to United to pull out of an obligation to sign him for £25m.

Villa were the next club to take him on loan, but he struggled to carve out a regular starting place in Unai Emery's team. He only contributed one goal and three assists in 39 appearances, although he did finish the campaign with a Europa League winners' medal.

‌



View 3 Images Jadon Sancho was last with Aston Villa (Image: Getty Images)

The Falcons are hoping the prospect of living in Dubai, which also offers tax-free earnings, and the club's top quality facilities may be enough to sway the likes of Sancho. The forward has a history with the popular Emirati city, having previously flown out there to recover from injuries in the past.

He is not the only big-name player who is without a club. Former England team-mate Raheem Sterling also failed to find a new team in the summer, as did ex-United colleague Paul Pogba and many others.

Sports.title: Argentina star hints at retirement after FIFA's brutal ban - 'We'll talk and see'
Sports.content:
Argentina star hints at retirement after FIFA's brutal ban - 'We'll talk and see'

Leandro Paredes was at the centre of attention for all the wrong reasons during the World Cup

View Image Leandro Paredes could retire from international football with Argentina (Image: Getty Images)

Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes has hinted he could walk away from international football, just days after Lionel Messi announced his own decision to step aside. His comments come in the wake of a chaotic World Cup final, where Argentina lost 1-0 to Spain and Paredes became embroiled in a mass post‑match brawl.

‌



The Boca Juniors man was seen trading blows at full‑time before shoving Spain's Gavi to the turf. FIFA's disciplinary committee has since issued a 10‑match ban and a £66,000 fine, while defender Nahuel Molina received a seven‑game suspension and the same financial penalty.

‌



Following an appeal from the Argentine FA, FIFA agreed to soften the impact of Paredes' punishment, allowing the suspension to be served across Class A friendlies as well as competitive fixtures.

‌



Argentina star slapped with 10-MATCH ban as FIFA announce World Cup punishments READ MORE :

Argentina World Cup fate decided after calls to ban finalists from next tournament READ MORE :

Yet he has suggested he has no plans to serve the lengthy suspension and is prepared to hold talks with Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni about his future.

"It's going to be difficult for me to stay with the national team," he admitted. "Because of the suspension as well, because of Leo's decision. It's going to be difficult for everything to carry on as before.

"I haven't discussed it with the coach yet, but we'll talk and see what decision I make."

‌



Messi announced his retirement from international football last month in an extensive statement saying goodbye to Argentina, with his final outing coming in the World Cup final defeat to Spain.

Paredes believes filling the void left by the Argentine icon will prove an enormous challenge.

‌



"Leo's legacy will live on forever because of what he achieved, for never giving up and for showing that dreams are hard won, pursued and, in the end, fulfilled," he added.

"We'd spoken in the final days of the World Cup about how the final would surely be his last match, but even so, we weren't prepared for that because of what he means to us."

Should he call time on his career, Paredes will bow out as a World Cup winner from Qatar 2022 and a two-time Copa America champion.

Sports.title: Argentina villain Leandro Paredes hints at international retirement after 10-game ban
Sports.content:
Argentina villain Leandro Paredes hints at international retirement after 10-game ban

Leandro Paredes was hit with a 10-game ban following his vile behaviour after Argentina’s World Cup final defeat to Spain and he has suggested that he may never represent his country again

View 2 Images Leandro Paredes has hinted he could retire from international duty (Image: Getty Images)

Argentina’s Leandro Paredes has hinted that he could retire from international duty after being slapped with a 10-match ban. The Boca Juniors midfielder sparked an ugly brawl after the South American nation’s World Cup final defeat by Spain.

‌



He shoved Spain star Gavi to the floor and faced three FIFA assault charges. After an investigation, FIFA handed him a 10-match ban and Paredes has now suggested that he might have made his last appearance for his country due that suspension, as well as Lionel Messi’s decision to hang up his boots for Argentina.

‌



“It's going to be difficult for me to stay with the national team,” Paredes said. “Because of the suspension as well, because of Leo's decision... It's going to be difficult for everything to carry on as before.

‌



“I haven't discussed it with the coach (Lionel Scaloni) yet, but we'll talk about it and see what decision I make.”

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Paredes, 32, has made 84 appearances in all for Argentina during his career, having made his debut back in 2017. He has also represented Roma, Zenit, PSG, Juventus and Roma.

‌



His comments come after he took aim at FIFA for their ban. He said: "That seems excessive to me. It is also strange that Gavi only received a suspension, even though he struck me in the chest. But well, that's how it is now. We now have to appeal against the sanction.

"The people who know about these things will see whether they can overturn it. For me, it is excessive and I think it can be reduced."

View 2 Images Paredes was involved in an angry brawl after the World Cup final (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Meanwhile, he has also commented on Messi’s decision to retire from international duty following the World Cup defeat. He said: “Leo's legacy will live on forever because of what he achieved, for never giving up and for showing that dreams are hard-won, pursued and, in the end, fulfilled.

“We'd spoken in the final days of the World Cup about how the final would surely be his last match, but even so, we weren't prepared for that because of what he means to us.”

Messi retires having made 207 appearances for Argentina in over 20 years and in that time, he has netted 125 goals. He helped the South American side to the World Cup in Qatar four years ago and has also won the Copa America twice. Messi has also claimed the Ballon d’Or on eight occasions during his lengthy career.

Sports.title: Premier League spending has become a laughing stock - implosion will surely follow
Sports.content:
Premier League spending has become a laughing stock - implosion will surely follow

Three Prime Ministers have come and gone since Manchester City were charged with breaking spending rules - and their spending this summer underlines the problem

View 3 Images Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak continues to spend, spend, spend (Image: Getty Images)

Richard Masters has had better weeks. Because he’s just been forced to sit and watch a product he runs eat itself from the inside out.

‌



A product which has spent millions on legal fees attempting to hold Manchester City to account. A club accused of breaking Premier League spending rules.

‌



So concerned with being found guilty, however, that it decided to spend the thick end of another £200million on new signings in the final hours of the summer transfer window.

‌



The world of football is still waiting to discover the outcome of the investigation into City’s alleged wrongdoings. So long, in fact, that in the time it has taken the relevant authorities to charge them with an offence and fail to reach a verdict, the UK has had three different Prime Ministers.

And none of them have had the wit to intervene in solving one of the most farcical events a game which England invented has ever been put through.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



In the meantime, City have taken the liberty of breaking their own spending record on a player not once, but twice, in the same summer.

View 3 Images Enzo Fernandez joined Manchester City for £125m on deadline day (Image: Manchester City FC)

It’s safe to assume the likes of Enzo Fernandez wouldn’t be joining City if they stood a serious chance of being punished with relegation to the lower leagues. It’s safe to assume Elliot Anderson wouldn’t be joining City if they stood a chance of being punished with relegation to the lower leagues.

‌



Get my drift? The integrity of the Premier League is becoming shambolic. It has become a laughing stock.

Liverpool broke their own transfer record twice last summer. Tottenham have spent more than £300m this summer and are still yet to win a league game.

View 3 Images Premier League CEO Richard Masters must know the integrity of his competition is being seriously questioned (Image: PA)

‌



Everton were willing to spend £10m on a loan fee for Joshua Zirkzee, who has been about as threatening at Manchester United as a wet sponge. Aston Villa won the Europa League, got into the Champions League, then decided to flog all their best players.

But signed someone in Alejandro Garnacho who stunk out United and then Chelsea. Go figure? The panic clubs show, which are run by executives being paid huge salaries in return for their so-called expertise, is frightening.

Who in their right mind thinks Fernandez is worth £125m? No-one, apart from those who treat hard cash like it's come from a Monopoly box. The same people who thought Anderson was worth £116m plus extras.

Article continues below

The footballing world has gone mad. City are not the only ones to blame. Top flight clubs have smashed their summer transfer record with over £3.3bn spent. More than half of them broke their transfer records in a window featuring four of the top flight's five most expensive ever deals.

Perpetuating a market which now sees clubs indulge in the kind of financial spending, which leaves those living in the real world wondering when it will all implode on itself.

Sports.title: Premier League transfers rated and slated after record-breaking summer of spending
Sports.content:
The summer transfer window is over and a record £3.49billion was spent across the Premier League, with over £500m of that coming just on deadline day itself.

Transfer fees of over £100m have become commonplace in the Premier League, with Enzo Fernandez (£125m from Chelsea to Manchester City), Bradley Barcola (£123m from Paris Saint-Germain to Liverpool), Morgan Rogers (£117m from Aston Villa to Chelsea), Elliot Anderson (£116 from Nottingham Forest to Manchester City) and Sandro Tonali (£100m from Newcastle to Tottenham) all reaching that mark.

Eleven of the 20 clubs in the Premier League broke their transfer record this summer, with City the biggest spenders, splashing out £458m on new players - another record for a single window. Chelsea (£349m) and Tottenham (£302m) went big this summer, while newly-promoted Ipswich spent a staggering £171m.

All this spending doesn't guarantee success. There are bound to be some high-profile flops this season, while some clubs managed to miss out on their targets altogether. Here Mirror Football's reporters give their takes on the busiest summer of spending ever.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

John Cross

Which team had the best window?

Manchester City. Enzo Maresca is trying to take over from Pep Guardiola, the best manager in Premier League history. He has to put his stamp on this team. They let legends go but have now brought in top, top quality. Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez, Ayyoub Bouaddi, Iliman Ndiaye and the rest. They also got good prices on their sales. They must be laughing all the way to the bank with Savio. City now look like a team equipped to challenge for the title again.

Which team had the worst window?

Everton. No wonder the fans are up in uproar. I was looking at Crystal Palace and Fulham … but the way it ended for Everton leaves us in no doubt. They lost their talisman in Iliman Ndiaye. They could not get Folarin Balogun over the line. They look short of numbers, they look worse off and it’s going to be hard for David Moyes to progress this season.

Best signing?

Bruno Guimaraes. Arsenal took Newcastle’s club captain, their best player and a ready made Premier League midfield superstar and got him for £75m. The best midfield just got better. It’s great value and also you are adding quality in a crazy market. If only Arsenal had got a left winger, too…

‌



View 8 Images Bruno Guimaraes was Arsenal's most expensive signing this summer (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA, Getty Images)

Most over-rated signing?

Savio. Tottenham paid how much?! They overpaid on a raft of deals but this one stuck out by a mile. Sandro Tonali for £100m was huge. Mateus Fernandes at £85m? Are you sure? Well, Savio who rarely did anything but flatter to deceive is the biggest price of all. Yes, they had to pay big to get good players after two successive 17th place finishes. But wow.

Best value for money signing?

Emiliano Martinez. He is fantastic business at £7.5m. A World Cup winner, a top class keeper at great value who is a game-changer for Chelsea. Robert Sanchez was not good enough and needed replacing. But they also have Mike Penders coming through. They can’t block his progress. This is just perfect and makes Chelsea potential title winners.

Which player are you most excited to see?

Bradley Barcola. The Frenchman has great stats for goals, assists and goal involvements generally. But if you actually watch him - remember watching games?! - then you will know that he can be frustrating and waste openings and chances. This is his big stage to deliver and I feel Liverpool are buying potential but also a player with a big to prove. And that’s good news. The other one is Mykhailo Mudryk. It’s a fascinating story.

‌



View 8 Images Bradley Barcola is Liverpool's big-money signing this summer (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Andy Dunn

Which team had the best window?

If there is an Agents XI out there, they stormed this category. The Premier League’s Deadline Day is their Christmas Day - and then some.

‌



It is tempting to see Manchester City as the big winners but any club that loses Rodri in a window cannot go lighting up the cigars. They might have got thumped at Old Trafford last weekend but I like the look of Ipswich Town’s business. Before their summer trading, they would have been seen as certainties for a relegation fight but the late capture of Zian Flemming completed a successful window.

Which team that had the worst window?

It was Everton, obviously. After all, the worst-window competition is the only thing they have won in the past three decades. And they have won it regularly. Even so, to leave the manager with only one striker - and that striker being Thierno Barry - was spectacularly inept.

But a special mention should go to their neighbours. It is hard to say a window has been bad for a team that signed a £123m player from Paris Saint-Germain but Bradley Barcola is not what Liverpool needed. A central midfielder and a right-back were needed and did not arrive.

View 8 Images Everton are very short after a miserable window (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



Best signing?

Considering the amount of money that is circulated, it is easy to be cynical about the transfer window, but there are some high-quality players moving for new challenges. Forget the price tag, Morgan Rogers is a brilliant acquisition for Chelsea and will ensure the anticipated title challenge materialises. James Trafford represents a game-changing piece of business for Leeds United but the signing that could well prove to be stellar is Ayyoub Bouaddi. It cost them enough money but Manchester City have a superstar on their hands.

Most overrated signing?

This is a fiercely-contested category with plenty of candidates - and that is before we look beyond Tottenham Hotspur. Enzo Fernandez has become the first player to be transferred twice for fees of over £100m, which considering the baggage he brings and his limitations, is staggering. Liverpool have paid plenty for Bradley Barcola and Nottingham Forest ’s £50m for Liam Delap was distinctly excessive. But the most overrated and over-priced has to be Sandro Tonali. At £100m, it is hard to know what Spurs were thinking.

View 8 Images Sandro Tonali is the most expensive of Tottenham's summer signings (Image: Getty Images)

Best value-for-money signing?

It is tempting to hail Emi Martinez - at £7.5m - as the bargain of the window but that might make the new Chelsea keeper even more unbearable, so we’ll park that. His fellow keeper, James Trafford, was an absolute snip at £40million for Leeds United and the same can be said for Hull City ’s £20m recruit in the same position, Konstantinos Tzolakis. But on the limited evidence of the season so far, Mamadou Sangare - who cost Brentford less than £40million - looks like the best pound-for-pound signing of the window.

‌



Player you're most excited to see at new club?

Manchester City fans will love Ayyoub Bouaddi’s style and although Evertonians will not be too buoyant right now, Hayden Hackney’s progress should give them some positivity over the coming months.

Abdul Fatawu has already proven to be good to watch with Ipswich and despite reservations about the size of his transfer fee, Bradley Barcola’s progress will be intriguing. But simply because we don’t know what to expect, it will be fascinating to see what Matias Fernandez-Pardo can do at Newcastle United.

Jeremy Cross

Which team had the best window?

Chelsea bucked their status quo of recent times and actually did some of the best business.

The signing of Morgan Rogers is one to excite the fans, as is landing Emi Martinez, while Chelsea also managed to off-load Mykhailo Mudryk on loan and recoup a whopping £125m for troublemaker Enzo Fernandez. The comings and goings have been astonishing, even by Chelsea's standards, but the net result is a stronger and more balanced squad, on the back of still making a profit.

‌



View 8 Images Morgan Rogers joined Chelsea from Aston Villa (Image: Getty Images)

Which team had the worst window?

Aston Villa have had a summer to forget, which is baffling considering they won the Europa League to reach the Champions League. Heroes have vanished in the shape of Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans, Martinez and Ollie Watkins. Villa have made some signings, but it's hard to see any of them replacing the quality which has gone. The strategy has been too drastic to allow Unai Emery to compete for a trophy and retain a place in the top four this season. Shambolic.

Best signing?

Emi Martinez has cost Chelsea just £7.5m, which in today's market, is peanuts. In return, Chelsea have got themselves one of the best goalkeepers in the business.

When it comes to signing keepers, Chelsea's recent record has been embarrassing. But they've struck gold this time. Martinez has all the experience in the world, having played in two World Cup finals and won one of them. He will make Chelsea much harder to beat.

‌



View 8 Images Emi Martinez has become the latest star to move from Aston Villa to Chelsea (Image: Getty Images)

Most over-rated signing?

The answer to this is simple. Savio runs him close, but Enzo Fernandez cost Manchester City a club-record £125m, which is mind boggling considering he's never challenged for a league title at Chelsea.

Fernandez is a decent footballer, but he's no Roy Keane or Patrick Vieira. What he actually is, is overpriced and overhyped. The fact he's now cost two English clubs more than £100m speaks volumes for how the game has lost its marbles, when it comes to the transfer market.

Best value for money signing?

Mamadou Sangare is starting to resemble the most underrated signing of the summer. The midfielder, 24, has joined Brentford from Lens in a club record £39m deal. But in years to come the fee might feel like some of the best money ever spent by a Premier League club. The Mali international is already making an impact in the Premier League and is guaranteed to prove a heck of a bargain.

‌



View 8 Images Mamadou Sangare has made a bright start at Brentford (Image: Getty Images)

Which player are you most excited to see?

Carlos Baleba hasn't come cheap, having joined Manchester United from Brighton in a £70m deal. But during his time on the south coast, Baleba showed signs he could go on to become a truly world-class midfielder. He appears to be the box-to-box star United have been missing in recent times. Could he become the next Roy Keane? United is a demanding environment, but it will be fun seeing how he adapts to his new surroundings at a club where times are never dull.

Sports.title: Shankland at the double as Rangers win at Falkirk
Sports.content:
Lawrence Shankland's stunning double secured back-to-back Scottish Premiership wins for Rangers with a 2-1 victory at Falkirk on Wednesday night.

Manager Derek McInnes was forced to watch from the stand at a rainy Falkirk Stadium as he began his touchline ban for comments made last season while in charge of Hearts.

It was his former Jambos captain who gave them the lead in style, collecting Djeidi Gassama's ball and smashing it into the net after eight minutes.

They were far from convincing and Kosta Nedeljkovic inexplicably knocked the ball into his own net to pull the Bairns level before half-time.

Falkirk then had the better of the chances and Jacob Murrell should have put them ahead on his home debut.

Aodhan Doherty wasted a brilliant chance after a mix-up between Gers keeper Ivor Pandur and Ross McCrorie, with the substitute then setting up his captain to sweep in the winner late on.

John McGlynn's remain without a league win and are only above pointless Kilmarnock, while Rangers are fifth on seven points from their four matches.

The key moments from the Falkirk Stadium

8: GOAL! Brilliant from the Rangers captain. Gassama sends the ball into Shankland, he switches onto his left before firing into the net.

16: CHANCE! Ross feeds the ball through to Fodrey in the box, but he can't get his feet sorted.

19: OFF THE POST! Kim denied by the woodwork.

24: SAVE! Kim close again! Bain reacts quickly to deny the Rangers newcomer, Raskin hits the side netting with the rebound.

44: GOAL! Falkirk are level. Ross sends in a cross, Nedeljkovic slides in to try and clear but instead puts it past Pandur.

48: SAVE! Fodrey gets his head to a cross but it's plucked out the air by Pandur.

51: CHANCE! Ross with a brilliant cross to the feet of Murrell but his effort lacks power and Pandur saves.

52: WIDE! What a chance for Shankland. Curtis lays it on a plate for the Rangers skipper but he somehow puts it past.

61: OVER! A brilliant chance for the Bairns. Murrell's header is deflected over the bar.

62: CHANCE! Falkirk should be in front! Murrell is one-on-one with Pandur after an awful pass from Fernandez, but his shot lacks power and the opportunity is gone.

78: WHAT A MISS! Doherty should have the ball in the after a mix up between Pandur and Curtis, but he gets it all wrong.

79: GOAL! A huge goal from the captain. Shankland collects McCrorie's pass, takes a touch then fires into the bottom corner.

'Classy' Shankland the difference

Former Rangers midfielder Scott Arfield on Sky Sports:

"At Hearts, Shankland had runners going in behind and I think you've got that now with this front four.

"Gassama looks like he's reinvented himself which obviously helps him and his two goals are just class.

"Shankland just touches it and he just knows where the goal is.

"It's like an easy wee golf shot and he just touches it, finishes it.

"Goals never move and he makes it look so easy and he'll continue to do that time and time and time again and that is why you bring him to the club because he is just a classy finisher."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ex-Rangers midfielder Scott Arfield was full of praise for Lawrence Shankland after his brace saw them win at Falkirk

Sky Sports' Kris Boyd:

"It's all about points to a certain point then you've got to start winning with performances.

"They've done enough to get over the line, but it's got to be better.

"It is all about winning but, at the same time, you've got to see signs of improvement and it was a slogfest out there for Rangers again.

"You're only as good as you're strikers and that's been the story tonight.

"You look at the chances Murrell missed at the other end, Rangers have got a clinical striker."

'Too scrappy' for McInnes

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rangers manager Derek McInnes was pleased with his side's resilience as they secured a hard-fought 2-1 win at Falkirk

Rangers manager Derek McInnes speaking to Sky Sports:

"Too scrappy for my liking. There were too many opportunities in the game for Falkirk.

"Lack of concentration in what you're trying to do really. If you're going to play the ball at the back and bring teams onto you it's to try and go somewhere with it.

"I just thought we ran up a cul-de-sac and gave away a few stupid little fouls. Just invites pressure and gives them a bit of encouragement.

"Sometimes that's where experience comes in.

"I'm not unhappy because we've won the game and we're in the back of winning at Aberdeen on Sunday.

"It's great to get another three points. I thought the effort for the team was great. As a team it was great.

"All the characteristics you want for a team coming away from home were there.

"It's all about winning games and hopefully now we can move on to Saturday and two home games now for us to look forward to.

"The window will be closed when we come into that game. I think that will be a godsend for me and for everybody else here."

Shankland: 'Winning breeds confidence'

Rangers captain Lawrence Shankland speaking to Sky Sports:

"Delighted to follow up from the weekend with another good result.

"We had quite a lot of moments around their box and I think we just snatched at a couple of things and made the wrong decisions.

"We knew we had to tidy up in the final third. I'll just keep shooting with my left foot!

"The scrutiny is up there at the moment, but I just had to stay confident and another chance would come.

"There's been a lot to sort out and take in. When you start winning games, it breeds confidence and everything feels a bit easier.

"We know we've got a lot to improve on with our performances, but we had some good moments and we'll take those positives."

McGlynn confident wins will come

Image: Falkirk manager John McGlynn

Falkirk manager John McGlynn speaking to Sky Sports:

"Absolutely gutted for the players, they put so much into the game to not get anything from it.

"We don't want to be known as the team who can play some nice football but not come out with points. We had some good opportunities in the second half that could have got us into a lead.

"I'm proud of the players for the performance they've put on and the effort they've put into the game.

"We go to Celtic Park and come out with a bit of credit, we get credit tonight but we want to get points out these games.

"We need to start winning games, but with the performance we have the encouragement that will come."
