Motherwell are third after Seb Palmer-Houlden, Alex Lowry and Dylan Levitt scored their first goals for the club in a 3-0 win against Dundee United.

St Johnstone salvaged a 1-1 draw in the Tayside derby against Dundee. Dundee seemed to have sealed the points when Charlie Reilly scored in the 87th minute, but St Johnstone’s Josh Fowler levelled in the 90th minute.

Sports.title: ‘A commodity’: Ismaïla Sarr’s agent wants respect for African players in transfer deals
Sports.content:
Ismaïla Sarr’s agent has claimed some African players are treated like “a commodity” after Crystal Palace turned down Liverpool’s approach for the Senegal forward and Lamine Camara’s move from Monaco to Chelsea broke down on deadline day.

Palace are understood to have rejected a bid from Liverpool for Sarr last week and insisted last season’s top scorer was not for sale. The 28-year-old, who missed the opening two matches against Everton and Manchester City after the manager, Pierre Sage, said he had picked up an injury, subsequently deleted all references to the Conference League winners from his social media accounts and is thought to have been disappointed by Palace’s stance.

Liverpool did not return with a bid on deadline day after deciding to keep Cody Gakpo, who was wanted by City.

Sarr’s Senegal teammate Camara was poised for a £47m move until Monaco backtracked on a club-to-club written agreement, leaving Chelsea fuming. The Ligue 1 side have said they pulled the plug on Camara’s transfer because they thought Folarin Balogun’s £40m move to Everton was back on after doubts over his medical.

Sarr’s agent, Diomansy Kamara, who won 50 caps for Senegal and played for Portsmouth, West Brom and Fulham, released a statement on Wednesday questioning the treatment of his compatriots.

View image in fullscreen The Senegalese midfielder Lamine Camara saw a move from Monaco to Chelsea fall through on transfer deadline day. Photograph: Valéry Hache/AFP/Getty Images

“The cases of Ismaïla Sarr and Lamine Camara must all interrogate us,” he said. “We have to get out of this logic where the African player can sometimes give the feeling that he is just a commodity: you buy it, you set its price, you negotiate its future and, too often, your will seems to go to the background. Our African players deserve respect. The respect of their work. The respect of their career. Respecting their ambitions. The respect of their voices.”

Kamara added: “The fact that clubs can sometimes have the final word is a reality of professional football. But one question remains: what about the career and the will of the player? The player must be able to be heard and respected in the decisions that determine his future. ‘Let’s never forget what’s important: behind every success, it’s the players who write history first.’”

Palace were contacted for comment. Monaco’s sporting director, Thiago Scuro, defended the Ligue 1 side’s actions in a press conference on Wednesday.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

He said: “Around 10pm, in our time here, maybe a bit earlier, Everton realised that OK there is no problem: ‘We are ready to do it. Let’s sign the contract.’ As soon as we got the information, yes, we did come back to Chelsea and told [them]: ‘OK, we have our deal there. There is no deal on Lamine.’ Because it’s also fair to do this. It’s also part of the game.”

He said it was unfair to portray Monaco as “the bad guys in the room”: “Everybody is very fair and nice in the football industry, just Monaco is not. Too much.”

Everton were left with only one recognised striker after Balogun changed his mind over the move to Merseyside and Scuro suggested the US forward was unhappy with how Everton had treated him over his medical.

Sports.title: Premier League transfer talking points: three things we learned from the data
Sports.content:
Premier League clubs have invested more than £3.4bn in players this summer, an increase of 11.9% on last year. There are three aspects of this enormous spending worthy of closer scrutiny.

Priorities on player age have changed

Premier League clubs are spending less on players in the peak 24-27 age band even though those players are increasingly the core of their selections.

As recently as 2021-22, 40% of minutes were taken by players at least 28 years old at the start of the season. That proportion has dropped each year, reaching 26.6% in 2025-26. The reliance on veterans has declined. The bulk of their lost minutes went to players aged between 24 and 27, which is now the dominant age band.

The spend on that key demographic has fallen by 23% since last summer though. Without Manchester City signing the 25-year-old Enzo Fernández for a British transfer record-equalling £125m shortly before the window closed, the drop would have been even greater.

Younger players account for some of the shortfall but a surprisingly high slice of it has gone towards older footballers. The Premier League has invested £323.3m in players aged at least 28, only around £50m shy of the outlay on this age range in the previous three summers combined (£370.5m). Their proportion of the total has not been as high for four years.

How much this increased spending on veterans affects the playing time figures depends in part on the selection decisions of Mikel Arteta. Arsenal signed two 28-year-olds for a combined £126m: Bruno Guimarães (£75m) and Ezri Konsa (£51m). Transfermarkt considers them to be the most expensive central midfielder and centre-back respectively aged over 27 in history.

The three most expensive Premier League signings of the summer before Fernández – Morgan Rogers, Elliot Anderson and Bradley Barcola – were 23 when their deals were completed. With only slightly less spent collectively on footballers who are 22, clubs have gone hard for players on the verge of entering their peak years rather than those in them.

The Premier League is becoming a closed shop

Perhaps the most notable aspect of transfer spending this summer is how much of it has remained within English football. Fourteen of the 19 signings that cost Premier League clubs at least £50m were made from within the division or from relegated West Ham. Where 30.2% of spending remained in the Premier League in summer 2022, the figure hit 39.3% this year.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

With the combined outlay growing by almost £1.5bn in that period, what appears a relatively small percentage shift becomes a significant figure in the accounts. The squad cost ratio rules are unlikely to stem this flow either, because clubs will be happy to sell for inflated fees that can almost only come from within the division.

Barcola was the oldest of the five costliest signings from overseas, with Matias Fernandez-Pardo and Jérémy Jacquet (aged 21), Johan Manzambi (aged 20) and Ayyoub Bouaddi (aged 18) completing the set. The Premier League is able to retain its top stars, its clubs exchanging them among themselves, while having the funds to hoover up the most exciting young talent from elsewhere.

Squad-building trends may be evolving in the Premier League, but the money is here and a significant portion of it is not going anywhere else. English football is starting to become an enclosed ecosystem.

The rest of Europe cannot keep up

Very few clubs across Europe come close to competing financially. The Premier League features a match this weekend between the top two teams in Europe for net spend and it isn’t Arsenal v Chelsea. Liverpool’s trip to Ipswich takes the honour.

The promoted sides have invested enormous sums to try to be competitive. They have all played League One football within the previous eight seasons, yet Real Madrid are the only club from another country with a higher net spend than Hull or Coventry.

The cream of the Premier League crop can probably only move within England. The transfer fee for Rogers (£117m) or Anderson (£116m) was above the net spend of 75 of the 76 top-flight clubs in France, Germany, Italy and Spain. Milan narrowly spent more than the cost of Sandro Tonali (£92.5m) net, but no other side beyond Madrid from mainland Europe did. Most non-English sides would have to have a clearout of talent to raise funds for a single elite player from the Premier League, which isn’t practical.

This financial dominance can be seen in continental competitions. Five English clubs have featured in the past eight Champions League finals, as many teams as the rest of Europe has provided in that time. The Premier League has supplied three of the past four Europa League finalists and three of the past four Conference League winners. This is unlikely to change when relegation favourites in England can outspend all but the very richest clubs overseas.

Sports.title: NFL rocked by tragedy as former star dies by suicide at 40... shortly after troubling final social media post
Sports.content:
NFL rocked by tragedy as former star dies by suicide at 40... shortly after troubling final social media post

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Former NFL star Alphonso Smith Jr. has reportedly died by suicide at the age of 40.

The former Detroit Lions cornerback passed away at a housing community in Florida on Wednesday, according to TMZ.

A chilling final Facebook post that appeared on Smith Jr.'s account earlier in the day referenced 'demons' and concluded by saying: 'THIS IS IT!'

‘I tried everything in my power to fight the demons behind the ones that someone put into ME!’ he wrote.

‘To my family, BABY, my MOM, my siblings, things happened to your boy, your brother while I was little that an older lady did onto me,’ he wrote. ‘As a result guys, I did the same onto others!’

Smith did not go into further detail about what happened to him or what he did to others, but did describe himself as someone who ‘needed help & did not get it.’

Former NFL star Alphonso Smith Jr. has reportedly died by suicide at the age of 40

A chilling Facebook post appeared on Smith Jr.'s account on Wednesday referencing 'demons'

Smith Jr. played college football at Wake Forest before being drafted by the Denver Broncos

He went on to blast himself as a ‘coward’ while apologizing to his children, parents, and friends.

'I am the WORST & I pray my soul rest in heaven for my heart is pure, but my BRAIN & experience is MESSED UP,' he added.

A Florida native, Smith Jr. played college football at Wake Forest from 2004 to 2008 before being selected by the Denver Broncos with the 37th overall pick in the 2009 NFL Draft.

During his college career at Wake Forest, Smith amassed 188 total tackles over four seasons to go with 21 total interceptions.

The Broncos traded him to the Lions in 2010 and he went on to play three seasons in Detroit before his NFL career ended after the 2012 season.

In total, Smith Jr. played in 42 NFL games and recorded 88 tackles and eight interceptions.

His death comes just over a month after Super Bowl champion Jordan Devey also died by suicide at the age of 38.

Devey's wife, Lindsey, shared the news in an emotional Instagram tribute posted on what would have been the couple's 15th wedding anniversary.

Former NFL star and Super Bowl champion Jordan Devey has died by suicide at 38 in July

'We have filled the walls of our homes and hearts with countless memories, joys, struggles, and triumphs,' Lindsey wrote alongside photos of the couple.

'We brought 4 beautiful children into this world that have your eyes, freckles, and compassion. You were our hero and our hearts ache in your absence. We love you. We miss you. And as you said in your last words to me, "we'll talk soon."'

A GoFundMe campaign launched on behalf of the family confirmed Devey died by suicide, leaving behind his wife and four young children.

'Tragically, Jordan took his own life, leaving his family to navigate an incredibly difficult and heartbreaking time,' the page reads.

'As they face overwhelming emotional and financial challenges, including mounting medical expenses, the community is coming together to support Lindsey and their children.'

Devey, who went undrafted out of Memphis in 2013, spent eight seasons in the NFL, playing for the Baltimore Ravens, New England Patriots, San Francisco 49ers, Kansas City Chiefs, Oakland Raiders and Buffalo Bills before retiring in 2021.

Over the course of his professional career, he appeared in 44 regular-season games and made 21 starts across stints with the Patriots, 49ers, Chiefs and Raiders.

If you or someone you know needs help, please call or text the confidential 24/7 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline in the US on 988. There is also an online chat available at 988lifeline.org.

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez risks wrath of Chelsea fans with claim he 'dreamed of joining a big club' after sealing £125m Man City move - as he joins Enzo Maresca in refusing to refer to Blues by name
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernandez risks wrath of Chelsea fans with claim he 'dreamed of joining a big club' after sealing £125m Man City move - as he joins Enzo Maresca in refusing to refer to Blues by name

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Enzo Fernandez has risked the wrath of Chelsea fans after claiming it was a dream to play for a club 'as big' as Man City after his £125million move, while only referencing the Blues as his 'previous club'.

Fernandez completed his transfer to Man City on deadline day, with the deal equalling the British transfer record fee paid by Liverpool to Newcastle for Alexander Isak last summer.

The Argentine had previously angered Chelsea supporters by flirting with a move to Real Madrid last season, leading to him being suspended by the club for two matches.

Fernandez had tried to explain his departure to Chelsea fans on social media by stating he had not been in a 'good place'.

'Life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions. I've said it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club. Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart,' Fernandez wrote.

'But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.'

Enzo Fernandez declared he 'always dreamed of being at a club as big as Man City'

Fernandez comments are likely to anger Chelsea fans, as he also referred to the Blues only as his 'previous club'

Fernandez had followed Enzo Maresca as not referring to Chelsea by name after joining City

Despite the sentiments, Fernandez followed Enzo Maresca in avoiding Chelsea by name after completing the move, with the Italian having referred to them as a 'different club' after joining Man City.

Fernandez also spoke of his dream of playing for a 'big club'.

'I'm really happy to be here,' Fernández said. 'I always dreamed of being at a club as big as City.

'I'm grateful for the opportunity. It's a very emotional moment for me and my family, to take this step at 25 years old, in a football career that I always dreamed of.

'I'm so happy to be here, enjoying these first few hours I've had at the club. I can already see just how big it is and, we will enjoy ourselves and win lots of things together.

'Manchester City have to win every trophy they compete for,' he said. 'In every competition we play in, we have to compete and win, because this club's history demands that.

'To be honest, from the first day they believed in me and called me to say they wanted me to join the club, I didn't hesitate for a second.'

When speaking about linking up again with Maresca, Fernandez added: 'He is a top manager, honestly, I had him at my previous club.'

They were incredible moments. I learned so much with him.

'I'm also grateful because he was very important in bringing me here. So it's a huge pleasure for me to work alongside him and enjoy it.

'To be honest, we were both very eager for it to happen, because it wasn't easy for me to be here today.

'But I know he also made a big effort, speaking to the club, and I'm grateful that he did that.

'It was a long few days, but in the end I'm here and I'm very happy to be joining this club.'

Sports.title: Clippers stripped of FIVE first-round picks and slapped with $30m fine as NBA rules on Kawhi Leonard secret payment scandal
Sports.content:
Clippers stripped of FIVE first-round picks and slapped with $30m fine as NBA rules on Kawhi Leonard secret payment scandal

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The NBA is stripping the Los Angeles Clippers of five first-round picks, issuing a $30 million fine to billionaire owner Steve Ballmer and suspending the former Microsoft CEO for one year following an investigation into improper payments to All-Star Kawhi Leonard, the league announced Wednesday.

The NBA has been investigating allegations that the Clippers circumvented the salary cap by funneling money to Leonard through an endorsement deal with companies including Aspiration, a green banking firm that has since gone bankrupt as its co-founder Joseph Sandberg admitted to defrauding investors out of $248 million.

'The investigation found a pattern of misconduct and multiple significant rules violations by the Clippers organization, a prior offender of the salary cap circumvention rules,' read the league statement.

Leonard will pay $700,000 in restitution for improper benefits he and his uncle/representative Dennis Robertson received from the Clippers and other organizations. However, the 35-year-old Leonard will not have any contracts voided by the league as a result of the NBA investigation.

Robertson, meanwhile, has been banned from any business dealings with the NBA.

Additionally, Clippers president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank has been suspened without pay for six months while president of business operations Gillian Zucker got a one-year ban.

The NBA is stripping the Los Angeles Clippers of five first-round picks, issuing a $30 million fine to billionaire owner Steve Ballmer

Kawhi Leonard came out of the year-long investigation with his earnings nearly intact

All punishments are binding, according to the league and players' union.

According to the a summary report prepared by law firm Wachtell Lipton, the Clippers violated NBA rules by 'initiating off-court income opportunities between Mr. Leonard and four companies doing business with the team.'

Those companies include Aspiration Partners, Boingo Wireless, Daktronics, and Lockton Insurance.

Additionally, the Clippers are accused of facilitating endorsement deals, inducing companies to enter into these agreements by offering other business with the team, and paying personal expenses on behalf of Leonard and his representatives.

Lastly, the team failed to report improper solicitations made on Leonard's behalf by Robertson.

Meanwhile, Leonard and Robertson were found to have pressured 'the Clippers to assist [Leonard] in obtaining off-court income opportunities, successfully obtaining those opportunities, and failing to reimburse payments by the Clippers for personal expenses,' according to the statement.

The Clippers recently agreed to trade Leonard back to Toronto, where he won an NBA title in 2019 before signing with LA. The deal was placed on hold as the league investigation continued over the summer, but as Leonard revealed in his statement, it appears he is now headed back to the shores of Lake Ontario.

NBA commissioner Adam Silver did follow some precedent with his punishment for LA

'Integrity and respect for this game are fundamental to who I am,' Leonard said in a statement issued by his agent. 'I accept full responsibility for lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle and regret the distraction this situation has caused the fans and my family.

'I entered into my contract with the Clippers as well as the agreements in question in good faith, fully committed to fulfilling my obligations and with no knowledge of any intent on anyone's part to circumvent the salary cap.

'For 15 years, my priority has been giving everything to my family, the game, and those I share the court with. As I return to Toronto, I am focused on what I can control, closing this chapter, and moving forward with a clean slate.'

There is precedent for at least a portion of the NBA's punishment for the Clippers.

NBA commissioner Adam Silver's predecessor, the late David Stern, similarly stripped the Minnesota Timberwolves of five first-round picks after discovering the team had circumvented the salary cap to improperly pay star forward Joe Smith in 2000. However, the Wolves were fined only $3.5 million at the time.

'The NBA's collectively bargained system for determining player compensation is a fundamental component of the basketball competition that the league oversees for the benefit of the teams and players and ultimately the fans,' Silver said in a statement. 'I am deeply disappointed by the flagrant violations of our rules and by the Clippers' institutional and leadership failures that led to this misconduct. The severity of the penalties reflects the seriousness of the violations.'

NBA commissioner Adam Silver's predecessor, the late David Stern, similarly stripped the Minnesota Timberwolves of five first-round picks for an improper deal with Joe Smith

The Timberwolves allegedly circumvented the cap to pay Joe Smith additional salary in 2000

Leonard’s arrival in his native Southern California was supposed to usher in a new era for the traditional NBA cellar-dwelling Clippers.

But in trying to lure Leonard, the Clippers traded for veteran All-Star Paul George from Oklahoma City in exchange for budding guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, who would go on to win an NBA championship and league MVP honors with the Thunder.

In total, the Clippers officially paid Leonard $291 million over seven seasons, not to mention the millions funneled through other businesses and the $30 million fine the team has incurred for those violations.

Regrettably, the Clippers don’t have much to show for the Leonard era. After reaching the Western Conference Semis and Finals in 2020 and 2021, respectively, the team has failed to win a playoff series since.

Leonard (seen here with Ballmer in 2019) initially signed a three-year deal with LA for $103m

The allegations against the Clippers first surfaced on Pablo Torre's podcast nearly one year ago.

Since then, NBA has been investigating the Clippers and Ballmer for allegedly facilitating an under-the-table side deal for Leonard that allowed the team to add other stars, such as Paul George. The team repeatedly denied the accusations, while Ballmer stated he had no knowledge of Leonard's alleged $28 million 'no-show' endorsement deal with the doomed financial services firm, Aspiration.

Torre made the claim against the Clippers by citing a 2025 bankruptcy filing that names the team and a company owned by Leonard under the list of creditors for Aspiration QFZ, LLC, a subsidiary of fintech and sustainability brand Aspiration Partners Inc.

Torre claimed to have contracts showing Aspiration QFZ, LLC entered into a $28 million 'no-show' agreement with Leonard's company, KL2 Aspire LLC, and later claimed - following a report from the Boston Sports Journal - that Leonard also received a separate $20million 'side deal' from Aspiration.

Ballmer invested $50 million in Aspiration through an LLC in 2021 as the team was also embarking on a $300 million deal with the green bank. Then, in April of 2022, Aspiration signed Leonard to a $28 million endorsement deal, which has been characterized as a 'no-show' job. Leonard did not publicly endorse Aspiration at any point.

Leonard joined the Clippers in 2019 and went on to sign two extensions with LA

Daily Mail obtained a federal bankruptcy filing showing unsecured claims of $30 million and $7 million for the LA Clippers and Leonard's company, KL2 Aspire LLC, respectively

The bankruptcy filing from federal court in Delaware, obtained by the Daily Mail, also shows unsecured claims of $30 million and $7 million for the Clippers and Leonard's company, KL2 Aspire LLC, respectively.

And while Ballmer said last year he was 'embarrassed' that he didn't pick up on any financial trouble from Aspiration, he defended his and the Clippers actions and said they 'weren't involved' in the company's deal with Leonard.

The team, as it pointed out in a statement, 'ended its relationship with Aspiration years ago, during the 2022-23 season, when Aspiration defaulted on its obligation.'

Furthermore, as reported by Torre, Aspiration QFZ's alleged payments to KL2 Aspire were sent to Robertson, Leonard's uncle and advisor, who was previously investigated by the NBA in 2019 for allegedly requesting impermissible benefits for his nephew and himself.

That 2019 investigation did not find any impermissible benefits going from the Clippers to Leonard or anyone working on his behalf.

A year later, a self-described acquaintance of Leonard and Robertson named Johnny Wilkes sued the Clippers, claiming he was still owed $2.5 million from the team for helping them to sign the former Spurs and Raptors star.

Wilkes, a self-described acquaintance of Robertson, claimed in the lawsuit that Ballmer would 'fund a $100,000,000.00 marketing campaign for Kawhi Leonard' and the uncle would get his own Southern California home if the All-Star forward agreed to sign with the Clippers.

That lawsuit was ultimately dismissed and neither the Clippers nor Robertson admitted to any wrongdoing.

Sports.title: Katie Boulter crashes out of US Open after being THRASHED by Karolina Muchova in worst Grand Slam defeat of her career - with Francesca Jones win the only silver lining for Brits
Sports.content:
Katie Boulter crashes out of US Open after being THRASHED by Karolina Muchova in worst Grand Slam defeat of her career - with Francesca Jones win the only silver lining for Brits

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Francesca Jones’ punchy three-sets win against Magda Linette for her first-ever US Open victory was the only silver lining as storm clouds over New York sparked a British washout, with Katie Boulter, Jacob Fearnley, and Jan Choinski all knocked out.

Qualifier Jones had won the first set of her delayed match late on Tuesday evening 6-4, when only the Briton’s admonishment to the supervisor that it was ‘bloody raining’ called an end to play. Stepping back onto court 17 hours later after a second rain delay, the downpour seemed to have washed away her promising form as the Polish veteran swiped the second set 6-1 in just 25 minutes.

Jones was down, but not out, and after a reset, she claimed the early break in the third. Not that the match was without late drama - as Jones was serving for the win when she requested a video review protesting accusations that the ball had bounced twice for 30-30. With the review in her favour, Jones wasted no time claiming the hard-fought victory, 6-4, 1-6, 6-3.

British No1 Boulter enjoyed a battling first-round win that had her praising her control of the ball in Flushing Meadows, but saw all early confidence drain away as she was despatched 6-1, 6-0 by Wimbledon finalist Karolina Muchova.

The seventh seed in New York, Muchova represented the most challenging of opponents for the world No62 and delivered on the promise of her ranking to fatal effect in just under an hour.

As rain drenched the outdoor courts, Boulter’s meeting with Muchova was promoted to Louis Armstrong, and both women appeared to struggle in the early stages with the hypnotic buzz of the crowd on the bustling show court.

Francesca Jones battled to a three set victory in her rain delayed first round match in New York

Katie Boutler was dumped out of the US Open with a 6-1, 6-0 defeat by Karolina Muchova

‘It's a hard balance. You really want atmosphere, and you want to play in a buzz and an energy. But today, I really let it get to me more than usual,’ Boulter admitted. ‘I'm not normally that aware of everything going on. I think it made me feel a little bit uncomfortable, which I have to deal with better.

‘We both have the same situation. We both have the same noise. It's not like it's just for me. It's both of us, and I have to deal with it better. And I think that's the crux of it.’

Just as Boulter had been broken in the opening game, she pinched back the next game on Muchova’s racquet. But it was the last one she would win. The Briton was broken again, and although she tested Muchova looking for the break back one more time in the fourth game, it was in vain. Muchova held, and any hope of a competitive match slipped through Boulter’s fingers.

It was a very, very good day for the Czech and a very, very bad day for her opponent. Muchova’s game style is a delight to watch, and she might have been playing an exhibition match against Boulter, whose touch deserted her as the Czech star settled in.

One particularly ropey attempt at a smash at the net in the first set summed up her afternoon – just as Boulter cantered up to bullet the ball past Muchova on the baseline, the ball sprang off her frame and out into the stands. The mishit set up Muchova’s break point for the first set, and she took it. Boulter’s only consolation on a difficult day will be that her loss comes against a strong contender for the title at this year’s tournament.

At least too, Boulter had not had to wait for her exit. Choinski had been scheduled for his first-round clash against Botic van de Zandschulp on Tuesday, only for a day of rolling scattered showers to have pushed the match back before its cancellation. As it was, he escaped a second rain delay by ten minutes as he was beaten 6-3, 6-1, 7-6(5) on a too-little, too-late afternoon.

German-born 6ft5’ Choinski credited his girlfriend Sophia, who acts as his coach for much of his time on the road, with attempting to keep him motivated throughout the match.

‘I had some break chances. I didn't use them. He broke my serve, and then from that point, it got tough,’ Choinski admitted after the match.

Fearnley also left his fightback too late as he fell to Tomas Martin Etcheverry 3-6, 3-6, 6-3, 3-6.

Sports.title: Chaos at Mohamed Salah's Trabzonspor as manager leaves less than a week after club BLOCKED his resignation following Europa League calamity
Sports.content:
Chaos at Mohamed Salah's Trabzonspor as manager leaves less than a week after club BLOCKED his resignation following Europa League calamity

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Mohamed Salah's new club Trabzonspor have confirmed the departure of head coach Fatih Tekke, less than a week after blocking his resignation.

Tekke had attempted to quit in the aftermath of Trabzonspor's 5-0 defeat by Hungarian side Ferencvaros in their Europa League play-off last week.

Tekke stated he was 'imposing this punishment on myself' after their exit.

The club responded that his resignation had 'not been accepted' and confirmed he would take charge of their match against Amedspor.

Trabzonspor then suffered a 2-1 defeat by Amedspor on Tuesday, leading to further talks between the club and Tekke, with an agreement reached for him to leave.

'As a result of the discussions held, we have mutually agreed to part ways with Fatih Tekke in line with Trabzonspor's interests and future-oriented goals,' a statement read.

Mohamed Salah's new club Trabzonspor have confirmed the departure of their head coach five games into the season

Fatih Tekke attempted to resign after their Europa League exit last week, but the club initially blocked the move

Trabzonspor were beaten in the league on Tuesday, with the club now agreeing to Tekke's exit

'Over the approximately 18-month period he served, Fatih Tekke added significant value to Trabzonspor.

'In addition to his contributions to the development of the players integrated into our squad during this time, he provided our club with important gains both in sporting and economic terms.

'By bringing the Turkish Cup to our trophy cabinet, he once again inscribed his name in Trabzonspor history.

'At the point we have reached today, we have arrived at a mutual understanding with our coach - who expressed that he could never accept his presence causing any harm to Trabzonspor in any way - that it is inevitable to chart a new roadmap by placing the club's interests above all else.

'We thank our coach for the effort, dedicated work, successes he achieved, and the value he added to our club up to this point.

'We wish Fatih Tekke success in his future career; as a member of the Trabzonspor community, I want to express that we will always remember him with respect for the beautiful emotions he brought to our club and the valuable legacy he left behind.'

Salah's new side have won just one of their opening three league matches, despite him scoring three times

In an additional update, the club announced Huseyin Cimşir would take charge of their next match with a process ongoing to appoint a permanent replacement.

Tekke's exit comes just five games into Salah's spell at the Turkish club, following his high-profile arrival in the summer.

The Liverpool legend has scored three times in five games for Trabzonspor, but his new side have won one of their opening three league matches, as well as being knocked out of the Europa League.

Sports.title: Bizarre moment US Open tennis star is handed CASH by a fan after winning her match
Sports.content:
Italian tennis star Jasmine Paolini was handed a bizarre good luck charm after her victory on Court 5 at the US Open on Wednesday.

In the early morning session on the outer court, Paolini managed to easily handle her fellow countrywoman Lucrezia Stefanini in straight sets, 6-4, 6-1.

After the match, Paolini was signing autographs and greeting fans when she was approached by a blonde woman wearing sunglasses.

The woman then produced a $2 bill, which Paolini initially thought was something she wanted signed. Instead, the spectator explained: 'It's for you. It's a $2 bill, they're rare, and they represent good luck.'

Paolini then thanked the fan, who advised the Italian to keep it in her bag the rest of the tournament.

It appears that some sort of good luck message was inscribed on the bill for the 19-seed in the women's singles bracket, who then held it up to the camera with a surprised look.

Italian tennis star Jasmine Paolini was gifted a strange good luck charm by a fan

A woman handed Paolini a $2 bill, noting that they're 'rare' and a token of 'good luck'

Paolini beat countrywoman Lucrezia Stefanini in straight sets to book a third-round spot

While not exactly rare – with 1.7billion $2 bills active in the United States – they're not commonly seen among the 55.6billion paper bills in circulation.

'I thought it was a nice gift and she told me this was the lucky one,' Paolini told the New York Post.

'[She said] 'keep it for yourself.' I was like, okay. I put it in the bag and it [will] stay with me. We'll see if it's going to work. That's the important thing.'

Paolini cruised to a victory in the second set after a close first frame which the 30-year-old won when Stefanini returned a serve into the net.

The world No. 21 has only gone as far as the Round of 16 at Flushing Meadows, which was accomplished back in 2024 – the same year she reached the final at both Roland Garros and Wimbledon.

With a spot in the third round secure, Paolini faces 16-seed Sorana Cîrstea of Romania.

Sports.title: Tiger Woods strikes deal and pleads no contest to reckless driving... after arriving at court with doting girlfriend Vanessa Trump
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Tiger Woods has pleaded no contest reckless driving and refusal to submit to a lawful test after striking a deal with prosecutors in the wake of his DUI arrest.

The golf legend was suited-and-booted as he arrived at court with girlfriend Vanessa Trump on his arm, looking stoic while wading through photographers outside the Martin County Court shortly after 8am on Wednesday.

Woods was pictured in the courtroom moments later, where he stood in front of a judge and changed his plea. He was originally charged with driving under the influence but has now pleaded no contest to a lesser charge of reckless driving.

As part of the deal, Woods will have his license suspended for five years.

The 15-time major champion was found at the scene of the crash in Jupiter, Florida, with two opioid tablets in his pocket, on March 27.

He has since spent time in rehab in Switzerland but had not been seen publicly since arriving back in America until last month.

Tiger Woods pleaded no contest to reckless driving at a hearing in Florida on Wednesday

Woods appeared puffy-eyed as he left the court alongside doting girlfriend Vanessa Trump

Vanessa led him back to a car after he had pleaded no contest and had his license suspended

According to police, Woods was driving at a high speed along a beachside road when his Land Rover clipped a tractor-trailer truck and rolled onto its side, causing about $5,000 worth of damage to the other vehicle.

He was able to crawl out of the car without any injuries before later admitting to officers he was looking at his phone and changing the radio at the time of the collision.

A Breathalyzer test did not reveal any alcohol in Woods’s system, but he refused a urine test, according to police.

The Sheriff’s report obtained by the Daily Mail said deputies found opioids in his pocket and he showed signs of impairment.

A previous hearing was held on August 4, following a July ruling that allowed prosecutors to obtain Woods' hospital records that were connected to the crash.

Martin County circuit court judge Darren Steele approved an agreement between the State Attorney's Office and Woods' legal team that allowed prosecutors to request records from the hospital that treated the PGA legend following his crash.

Back in May, Steele approved a similar agreement granting prosecutors access to Woods' prescription medication records from his Palm Beach pharmacy between January 1 and his March crash.

Prosecutors and Woods's attorney have agreed to a protective order that limits the release of any hospital or prescription records to the State Attorney's Office, law enforcement, state experts and the defense.

Woods appeared puffy-faced as he arrived for his change-of-plea hearing in Florida

Vanessa was front and center inside the court as Woods pleaded no contest to reckless driving

Woods in the back of a police cruiser after being arrested on suspicion of DUI in March

Woods was closing in on a return to golf and was widely expected to compete at The Masters in the days before the crash.

He hasn't competed since the 2024 Open Championship at Royal Troon in Scotland and has since undergone surgery to repair a torn Achilles as well as a seventh back procedure.

Woods' legal problems have since been put into perspective by Vanessa's cancer diagnosis. She revealed her bout with an unspecified form of breast cancer back in May.

The March crash marked the fourth major driving-related incident of Woods's adult life.

Five years earlier, when Woods rolled another SUV down a steep embankment in California, he did not face any accusations of driving under the influence. Instead, the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department claimed Woods was driving at around 80mph, nearly twice the legal limit, at the time of the crash.

Witnesses told TMZ that Woods appeared agitated and impatient while leaving a golf tournament parking lot in the moments before the crash.

Woods after his arrest on suspicion of driving under the influence (DUI) in Jupiter, Florida, on May 29, 2017. He later pleaded guilty to reckless driving

Woods changed his original not guilty plea in the wake of his DUI arrest back in March

Vanessa with him and her 19-year-old daughter Kai back in March

Woods was never charged in 2021, but he wasn't so lucky in 2017, when he was found by Jupiter police about 15 miles from his home. Officers said they found him unconscious in his Mercedes-Benz, which was parked awkwardly on the roadside at around 3am.

Upon closer inspection, they noticed damage to his vehicle.

Woods didn't have any alcohol in his system, but later tests found the active ingredient for marijuana, two painkillers - Vicodin and Dilaudid - the sleep drug Ambien and the anti-anxiety drug Xanax.

He later claimed he had been self-medicating for pain caused by his fourth back surgery and insomnia. Woods did not specifically address the marijuana issue and he wasn't found with the drug in his possession.

Woods pleaded guilty to reckless driving and received a year of probation, a $250 fine and was ordered to undergo 50 hours of community service. He was also banned from drinking alcohol during the probation.

In July 2017, Woods completed a private program to address his dependency on painkillers.

Woods stands alongside his lawyer to face County Judge Darren Steele on Wednesday

In April the Daily Mail broke the news that the golfer would leaving the country 'imminently'

The golf great flipped his Land Rover clean onto its side during his accident in Jupiter

'I will continue to tackle this going forward with my doctors, family and friends,' he tweeted at the time. 'I am so very thankful for all of the support I've received.'

Woods' most notorious car crash took place in 2009, when he rammed his Cadillac Escalade into a fire hydrant, tree and several hedges near his home.

He was treated for minor injuries and received a ticket for careless driving, but while he thanked his then-wife Elin Nordegren for getting him out of the car, there were lingering doubts about the story. After all, it was only days earlier that the National Enquirer claimed he'd had an affair with Rachel Uchitel, a 9/11 widow and New York nightclub manager.

The alleged details of the November 27, 2009 crash were ultimately included in the best-selling biography by Jeff Benedict and Armen Keteyian, titled Tiger Woods.

Sports.title: Custom kits, $400,000 jewellery and battling online trolls: How Naomi Osaka and Aryna Sabalenka's eye-catching fashion statements are helping them transcend tennis
Sports.content:
For Naomi Osaka, preparations on the eve of this year’s US Open were a little unorthodox.

As well as hitting the practice court and allowing time for rest and recovery, the four-time Grand Slam champion prowled a deserted Billie Jean King National Tennis Center looking for backdrops for a series of glamorous high-fashion photoshoots. Dressed by Hollywood superstar Zendaya's stylist Law Roach, Osaka posted on Arthur Ashe, by concession stands, and, most improbably, in the creaky media workroom.

All of this was building to the ultimate spotlight. As she has done at this year’s Australian Open, Roland-Garros, and Wimbledon, Osaka walked out for her first-round match in a custom ensemble designed for the Grand Slam, this one inspired by basketball legend Allen Iverson and also styled by Law. Although she secured the necessary win, the match wasn’t nearly as memorable as the outfit, a sleeveless hoodie embroidered with burnt press clippings, over a full tulle ballgown skirt.

With her walk-on outfits this season, variously inspired or compared to jellyfish, the Eiffel Tower, Lucy Liu in Kill Bill, and the Japanese art of paper-cutting, Osaka has created a feverish atmosphere around the moment she steps onto court. Loved or loathed, the walk-on outfits have become part of Osaka’s package, as questioned and dissected by the media and online as her forehand - or maybe more.

But Osaka isn’t alone in using fashion to distinguish herself from her peers off the court. World No1 Aryna Sabalenka played her first round match wearing a staggering $400,000-worth of jewels on her neck, wrist, and ears. The ‘Silhouette’ suite was made for her by her jewellery sponsor Material Good, and is the fourth of four specially-designed sets made for Sabalenka to wear at each of the Grand Slams. Wimbledon’s, naturally, featured emeralds.

For players at the very top of the game, tennis is not the only thing fans are looking for on-court at the majors.

Naomi Osaka honoured NBA legend Allen Iverson, with her dramatic on-court ensemble at the US Open on Monday night in New York

Osaka donned Iverson's famed arm sleeves and headband as part of her latest fashion statement, which is distinguishing her off the court as well as on it

Osaka is not alone in delivering a fashion statment on court, with world No1 Aryna Sabalenka having been dripping in coloured gemstones as she stepped onto court in New York

The set is worth over £295,000 ($400,000) and reflects New York City's multicultural heritage

The headline-catching choices that both Sabalenka and Osaka have made are increasingly allowing them to transcend tennis, crossing into the mainstream with fashion and pop culture fans dissecting their tournament-specific looks on social media. They’re ripe for the water cooler too: tennis lovers in mothballs might clutch their pearls, but people are tuning in, with passing interest, to see what Osaka is wearing this time, or leafing through articles about Sabalenka in Vogue, TIME, or Vanity Fair.

Osaka has a particular platform for making sure she stands out on court, as the only active Nike player with a unique deal that affords her custom tennis kits. So exclusive that they’re not always for sale, her Australian Open dress sold out in the blink of an eye. Sabalenka, while given a one-of-one colour choice, isn’t so lucky, as she found out at this year’s Roland-Garros. After debuting her kit on TikTok in a splashy reveal for her followers, she was pipped to the court when world No93 Oksana Selekhmeteva wore the black and red mesh ballet-style dress in her defeat to Marta Kostyuk, purchased off the rack.

‘Let’s wait for 2027, because that will be sick!’ Sabalenka teased when asked about not having exclusive looks at the 2025 WTA Finals. For another year then, she must grin and bear it.

Of course, fashion statements do not solely benefit those wearing the clothes. Coco Gauff is an ambassador for Italian high-end fashion brand Miu Miu, who pounced on the opportunity to partner with her kit sponsor New Balance on a number of custom outfits since 2025 - a move that might have Gucci ambassador Sabalenka wishing Nike was a little less stringent in its aversion to partnerships. The American star wore one of these at this year’s Wimbledon, landing her on a raft of ‘best dressed lists’, with fellow player Jelena Ostapenko telling Daily Mail Sport it was her favourite of the tournament. More pertinently, it boosted Miu Miu’s visibility and ties to a sport which is only growing in popularity and cultural prominence.

Traditional sponsors are also leaning in to the power of a unique fashion moment can have for a growing star. Nike has singled out rising Filipina talent Alexandra Eala for special recognition, as she quickly becomes one of the most famous faces in her region as the first player from the Philippines to break into the top 20 and make the fourth round of a major. At Wimbledon last year, she was given a white hair accessory in the shape of a sampaguita - her country’s national flower - to wear for her Centre Court debut. In New York this week, she stepped onto court to play an exhibition match during Fan Week wearing trainers customised with a tag which commemorated her first WTA title, which she won at the start of the month in Washington.

Even the men’s tour are getting in on the action. World No14 Lorenzo Musetti was the picture of Italian elegance when he admirably sported a white leather Bottega Veneta bomber jacket for his Wimbledon walk-on as temperatures hit 35 degrees in south London. German outfitter Hugo Boss looked to outdo this the following year by providing Taylor Fritz with a full white suit to step onto court in, the Roger Federer throwback only a little dented by the fact that the trousers were Velcro tear-off for ease. There are still teething problems on that side of the draw, with Matteo Berrettini’s Boss outfit banned by Wimbledon for being the wrong shade of cream.

Osaka made a fashionable run-up to the tournament with a series of photoshoots around the Billie Jean King National Tennis Centre, including improbably in the media workroom

Osaka has garnered attention with a series of daring outfits at Grand Slams, starting with one some fans compared to a jellyfish with its billowing veil at the Australian Open

Osaka was inspired by the Eiffel Tour for Roland-Garros, while she was able to get creative with Wimbledon's strict dress code

Coco Gauff's Wimbledon outfit, a custom one produced by her sponsors Miu Miu and New Balance, was lauded

Sabalenka had to defend her US Open outfit which was branded 'trashy' by critics online, but appeared in a different version for her first round match

But as anyone making a fashion statement knows, execution can be hit or miss and the online fashion police are unafraid of twisting the knife. In New York, Sabalenka has had to stand firmly by her night-session dress, which was dubbed ‘trashy’ by critics online.

‘I love that it’s different. I love that this outfit is bold,’ Sabalenka said before the start of the tournament. ‘Whatever people saying on Internet, I heard they probably didn't like it.

’It’s like it's funny for me, because when Nike was pretty simple and standard, they were complaining. When Nike went really cool and fun and trying to get back, they always complain.’

Either way, people are talking about it. In 1989, Andre Agassi was mocked for taking part in a Canon advert where he declared ‘image is everything’. No one’s laughing now.

Richarlison was heavily linked with a return to former club Everton. The two clubs were in negotiations over a potential move for Iliman N'Diaye, who eventually completed a deadline day move to Manchester City.

Amid the speculation, Richarlison appeared to hit out at Spurs in a statement released on Instagram. Despite the English transfer window being closed, it seems that the striker has made a decision over his future.

Sports.title: Man United handed £70m boost after 'rare' Marcus Rashford situation
Sports.content:
Man United handed £70m boost after 'rare' Marcus Rashford situation

Marcus Rashford has been given a fresh opportunity at Manchester United after his Old Trafford career appeared to be over.

View Image Marcus Rashford has been given a new lease of life at Man United (Image: Matt West/Shutterstock)

Manchester United have been handed what Nicky Butt calls a £70million Marcus Rashford boost, with the former midfielder underscoring the extraordinary circumstances behind the winger's return. The England international has been offered a second chance at Old Trafford, and supporters made that clear with a loud, enthusiastic welcome as he stepped back onto the pitch for the first time in 18 months.

‌



Seeing Rashford embraced by thousands of United fans, back in club colours and training alongside his teammates, is a scene few believed would ever materialise again. The clearest sign his United story was over came last summer, when his No.10 shirt was handed to Matheus Cunha, seemingly closing the chapter for good.

‌



Before this season kicked off, Rashford had not played a competitive game for United since December 2024. But the club opened the door to a reintegration during pre‑season, and he is now firmly within Michael Carrick’s plans, featuring in both of their opening Premier League fixtures.

‌



Rashford will stay at the club until at least January when the window reopens when clubs can make an approach.

Discussing the circumstances, former United midfielder Nicky Butt expressed his hope this marks the beginning of a redemption arc for the winger. He told Midnite: "Are we witnessing the start of a good redemption story with Marcus Rashford? You'd like to think so.

"It'd be a really nice story for someone to have had such a bad time for a couple of years at United. He's come through the academy as a superstar and potentially could have been should be up there with the likes of [Kylian] Mbappe. He went away, did okay at [Aston] Villa, went away, did well at Barcelona, and then it went sour for him.

‌



"The reception he's got is amazing. You think about it because there's not many clubs that give a player a reception like that when he's walked away from the club for whatever reason. He's back there now. He's out and out on the one of the top players in Europe on his day."

"But the thing with Marcus is he has to be on it every single minute of the day because the minute he steps his foot off the pedal - there will be critics around the club. It will happen. Ex-players will be saying 'Is he really going to be there? Is his heart there?' But he is without doubt a £70m signing to come back."

Rashford departed United after losing his place under former manager Ruben Amorim. The Portuguese boss axed him in December 2024 and issued a stark warning to the forward, stating: "Our team should be so much better with Rashford but he has to change.

"If he changes, we are more than welcome to put in a talent like Rashford and we need it."

Sports.title: Lazy recruitment and transfer addiction: Inside 'wild west' £3.4bn window with agent Sky Andrew
Sports.content:
After a record-breaking summer transfer window, the dust has finally settled on a Premier League market that has reached extraordinary financial heights.

More than £3.4billion was spent, comfortably surpassing last season's record of £3.1bn, while four of the division's five most expensive transfers - including Enzo Fernandez's British transfer record-equalling £125m move from Chelsea to Manchester City - took place this summer.

Eight deals worth £80m or more were completed, while 14 of the 20 Premier League clubs spent more than £100m. Six clubs surpassed £200m and three spent more than £300m. In total, £506m was spent on deadline day alone, up from £391m last year.

So how did the transfer market reach such unprecedented levels?

‌



Veteran agent Sky Andrew, the negotiator behind Sol Campbell's infamous 2001 cross-London switch from Tottenham to Arsenal, offered an insight into the forces driving the modern transfer market, as well as the changing dynamics behind the deals themselves.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Tottenham's 'bank-rolled' mega spree

Tottenham's unprecedented £300m-plus outlay - including the £100m purchase of Sandro Tonali and the £85m capture of Matheus Fernandes - following back-to-back 17th-place finishes, was one of the defining stories of the summer.

Andrew believes the scale of the spending illustrates how clubs can use financial facilities to fund major investment.

‌



"It is definitely 'all brakes are off' - but it's all brakes off with the banks as well. You can't spend that much money without having facilities with the banks," Andrew said speaking on the Mirror Football podcast.

"Spurs are a fantastic business, so the board looks at what the club and stadium are worth, goes to the banks for a facility of half a billion, and spends it. But you can't have £300m-£400m worth of players and none of them have residual value - they either need that or Champions League football to balance the books."

Andrew also believes Tottenham's aggressive approach changed the behaviour of their rivals, with other clubs responding to Spurs' early activity.

"Spurs were a surprise package... It was like a 100-metre race and Spurs got off to a blinder. What the fans are used to is a lot of chat and no spend, but they definitely affected the market... When they said 'we're spending,' wow. All the other clubs were like, 'Well, we need to get down to business.'"

‌



View 3 Images Savio joined Tottenham in an £85m deal that raised a lot of eyebrows (Image: Chloe Knott/Tottenham Hotspur FC/Shutterstock)

Lazy recruitment

Andrew believes some of the biggest clubs are increasingly willing to let smaller sides do the hard work of identifying emerging talent before swooping in once a player has established himself.

"A lot of big clubs are just saying, 'we're not going to recruit at the stage that Brighton and Bournemouth are going to recruit.' They wait for Brighton and Bournemouth to get the players, bring them in, and then pay attention [paying premium fees later]."

He added: "Football is now with the big clubs... the bigger your turnover, you can spend 85 per cent on salaries and transfers. Obviously, if you're a big club, then you're spending more than most of the other clubs."

‌



Player psychology and fan expectation

Behind the eye-watering transfer fees, Andrew believes there is another powerful force driving the market: the psychology of the players themselves.

"I can't explain to you how much of a honeymoon period that excitement of a move is for a player. It can become addictive. This is why a lot of players move a lot - because it's addictive. Players just want to feel wanted."

He also believes supporters can play a significant role in shaping a club's transfer strategy, particularly when they are demanding reinforcements.

"I think for the fans, to see the club having a go, I think that's very important to the fans. So they're having a go. In the past years when they've been flitting with relegation, the fans are moaning, but this year you've got to say, 'Okay, we're giving it a go.'"

‌



View 3 Images Bradley Barcola joined Liverpool from PSG in a £123m deal (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

The death of transfer rules and the rise of 'tapping up'

The traditional process of club-to-club negotiation has also changed significantly, with Andrew arguing that the rules governing how transfers are conducted have failed to keep pace with the modern market.

"The biggest change that I've seen is a blatant disregard of the rules in terms of it having to be club to club," Andrew said. "Now you're seeing it reported: players' wages have been agreed with the buying club, everything's been agreed, now the clubs have got to agree. That's not how it's supposed to happen... the authorities have just agreed that 'we can't stop this.'"

He also believes the growing number of intermediaries involved in transfers has made the process increasingly complicated.

‌



"In the early days when I started as an agent, if you represented a player, no one else got involved. But now in football, there are so many agents, brokers... very rarely do you see a deal that has just one agent," Andrew said. "You've got three or four agents getting involved, representing clubs, managers, players. A lot of clubs don't get clear information, and that causes a problem."

He added: "Football's big business and it's a small world, and the gossip that goes on behind the scenes is unbelievable. Agents talking to agents, clubs speaking to clubs... the club selling the player almost has got no say in it.

"Unless there's a complaint made, then the deal just goes through. You'll find that very few complaints are being made because if the club selling the player gets the money they want, they too just let it fly."

Sports.title: Atletico Madrid slammed for Julian Alvarez treatment after failed Arsenal move
Sports.content:
Atletico Madrid slammed for Julian Alvarez treatment after failed Arsenal move

Arsenal remained keen on a move for Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez deep into the summer transfer window but the Gunners were unable to find an agreement for the Argentine forward

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez remains at Atletico Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

Barcelona star Dani Olmo says he ‘doesn’t understand’ Atletico Madrid’s treatment of Julian Alvarez after denying him a ‘dream’ move. The Argentine forward was of interest to Arsenal and Barcelona heading into the final days of the window.

‌



Mikel Arteta had approved a switch to the Emirates Stadium, but only if Alvarez himself was open to the move. Arsenal faced serious competition from Spanish giants Barcelona, who had seen a number of bids for his services turned down.

‌



Atletico Madrid then released a statement saying that they would not be doing business with their domestic rivals and Alvarez would stay at the Metropolitano. And Barcelona star Olmo has now taken aim at Atletico for their treatment of the forward.

‌



Speaking to Spanish outlet Mundo Deportivo, the Spanish playmaker said: “Julian is a great player, a great ‘9’, one of the best in the world without a doubt, but that’s football.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“Understand it? I don’t. In the end, we all have our dreams. I think Julián was also clear about that,” the Barcelona star added.

‌



“He fought for his dreams, but ultimately there are also other external situations that one can’t control. In that sense, that was one of them, it goes without saying. But life goes on. This doesn’t stop.”

While neither Barcelona nor Arsenal managed to sign Alvarez, the pair actually ended up doing business together, with the Catalans instead sealing a move for Gabriel Jesus.

And while the Brazilian was second-choice, that is not something he minds too much. Speaking at his unveiling, the former Arsenal star said: "A week ago I received a message that it could happen.

‌



View 2 Images Gabriel Jesus moved to Barcelona instead of Julian Alvarez (Image: Getty Images)

“When I started to think it was a real possibility, I was so excited. Now I can't wait to start training and playing.

"It doesn't annoy me [being Plan B to Alvarez], it doesn't bother me. What annoys me is if people say I'm a bad guy, which has never happened in my life - or if I am not playing football, that bothers me.

‌



"I have the chance to play for Barcelona, a chance I had 10 years ago and now life has offered me that opportunity again."

"I took a significant salary drop, but it's a dream to be here," Jesus added. "But it wasn't just me who had to make an effort to get the transfer over line, Barca also played their part.

"If you had asked me one month ago, I would have said it was unlikely this would happen. At 29, I didn't think I would have the chance to come to Barca.

Article continues below

"The last two years have been really complicated after the knee injury. I was out of the game for almost one year, but it's in the past. I feel good physically now. I recovered well, returned to action for Arsenal and I am 100 per cent ready to play and give my all."

Sports.title: Man Utd had 'very big' offer rejected in final hours of summer transfer window
Sports.content:
Man Utd had 'very big' offer rejected in final hours of summer transfer window

Manchester United were linked with an interest in the England youth international in the final weeks of the transfer window.

View 2 Images Manchester United made a deadline day attempt to sign Leicester City midfielder Louis Page. (Image: Plumb Images, Leicester City FC via Getty Images)

Leicester City manager Russell Martin has confirmed that the club turned down 'a lot of money' from Manchester United for young midfielder Louis Page. The 18-year-old was linked with a deadline day move to Old Trafford.

‌



It had previously been confirmed by Martin that the Foxes had turned down a bid from United for Page. With the deadline approaching on Tuesday, the Red Devils made a second attempt to sign the England youth international.

‌



Any potential late deal was complicated by Leicester's League One game against Plymouth on Tuesday night. Amid the talk ramping up over his future, Page was still included in the starting line-up for the match at the King Power Stadium.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury losing patience over Anthony Joshua fight - 'You're a coward!'
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury losing patience over Anthony Joshua fight - 'You're a coward!'

Fury, 38, and Joshua, 36, signed separate contracts to fight each other earlier this year but Joshua's deal included the stipulation that the clash must take place in the UK

View Image Tyson Fury speaks out (Image: Getty Images)

Tyson Fury has branded Anthony Joshua a "coward" as the row over the venue for their fight rumbled on.

‌



Fury, 38, and Joshua, 36, signed separate contracts to fight each other earlier this year. Joshua's deal included the stipulation that the clash must take place in the UK with Wembley the frontrunner. But Netflix and the showdown's Saudi Arabian backers want the fight - which is pencilled in for November 20 - moved to New York. Joshua is prepared to back down if a series of demands are met.

‌



But no deal has been agreed - and Fury claims he is running out of patience. "There is still no deal done and it's getting quite tiring," he said. "I've been down to fight in every location that's been mentioned; England, Ireland, Vegas, New York, back to England, back to Ireland, back to New York.

‌



Tyson Fury makes major Anthony Joshua fight announcement READ MORE :

Anthony Joshua closer to Tyson Fury fight deal after key demand met READ MORE :

"I've said yes every time with zero stipulations. The facts are, I feel like you're being a coward. I feel like you don't want to fight and you're just conning everybody. I feel like you've been doing that for years. You've had many opportunities to fight me, but deep down you never really wanted it. So let's see if you're going to man up the final time.

"Let's f***ing fight. It's a boxing match; you've been banjoed before plenty of times. You've been knocked spark out a few times, so what? What's the worst that can happen? I'm going to f***ing chin you, 100 per cent, but it's nothing that hasn't been done before!"

Article continues below

Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn revealed earlier this week that one of Joshua's key demands - payment of his purse for his win over Kristian Prenga in July - had been met. "We're all good from the last fight, and we're all moving forward amicably," he said. "We don't want to do the fight in the US, but we also understand it has to work for everybody.

“We've been banging our head against the wall on that for the last two months. We've set out our position, mainly in concern to the tax situation that will deplete his net purse by going to America, which can be rectified. There's nothing unreasonable in there. If they want it in the US, they'll sign it. If not, we'll be very happy, and we'll do it in the UK.

"We are speaking multiple times a day but we are running out of time if they want to do the fight on November 20. We will need to make a decision this week."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
