Sports.title: Frank Martin Believes Recent Struggles Will Attract Contenders
Sports.content:
That inactivity left him 1-1-1 across his last three appearances, including a knockout loss to Gervonta Davis and a draw with Nahir Albright. Those results removed much of the fear that once surrounded him, but Martin views his reduced standing as useful bait.

“There’s going to be some fighters who feel that they may take a chance to fight me just off the last performances or whatever and think it’s sweet or it’s an easy fight. They’re just going to put me in the seat that I want to be in. I would like to fight Lindolfo Delgado. I like that fight right there,” Martin said during Wednesday’s DAZN-streamed press conference.

The strategy works only if Martin’s decline has been exaggerated. He remained competitive with Davis through six rounds before one of boxing’s best finishers caught him in the eighth. That loss alone did not prove Martin was finished, but the Albright draw made it harder to dismiss his recent difficulties.

Buddy McGirt has been brought in to correct some of the habits behind those performances. Martin backed himself into a corner against Davis and surrendered the space needed to escape the finishing combination. Albright also troubled him when Martin allowed himself to be pushed toward the ropes.

McGirt traditionally emphasizes a firm jab, defensive responsibility, and movement away from dangerous positions. The first test of their partnership will be seeing if Martin holds the center instead of depending on last-second reactions near the ropes.

Moving to 140 pounds adds another uncertainty. Martin’s speed and counterpunching should travel with him, but his power was never overwhelming at lightweight. Larger fighters may become more aggressive if his punches do not earn their respect. More frequent appearances may sharpen his timing, although they will also show quickly how his offense works against naturally bigger opposition.

Flores would provide a useful comparison if he receives the October fight. He pushed Delgado to a split decision in 2024, giving Martin an opportunity to measure himself against the opponent he wants. Struggling with Flores would weaken Martin’s case for facing Delgado, while a decisive performance would strengthen it.

Delgado remains the more difficult technical test. He is patient, disciplined, and rarely gives away clean countering opportunities. Martin would need sustained activity to win rounds rather than waiting for isolated openings.

The former lightweight contender wanted fighters to stop avoiding him. He may get his wish, but another poor showing risks turning him from a contender into a stepping stone.

Sports.title: O’Shaquie Foster Calls Emanuel Navarrete a Weight Bully
Sports.content:
Foster recognized the bait. Rather than promise a stationary slugging match, he argued that Navarrete is accustomed to imposing himself on physically inferior opposition.

“He’s trying to talk me into sitting there banging with him. That’s not going to happen. I’m going to control the fight, and I’m going to dominate him. If he gets too crazy, I’m going to put him to sleep. He better remember I’m not them little boys he’s been fighting, them little kids. He’s been weight bullying all these people. I’m not that,” Foster said during the DAZN-streamed press conference.

The accusation carries more substance than the usual prefight insult. Navarrete was at his most destructive at 122 pounds, where his height, reach, punch output, and physical strength allowed him to overwhelm smaller opponents. Those edges became less pronounced at featherweight and have continued shrinking at 130.

His dominant stoppage of reigning IBF champion Eduardo “Sugar” Núñez in their February unification was treated as proof that the old Navarrete had returned. Núñez held a world title, but his record remained thin, and his basic slugging style was made for Navarrete. He came directly at him and accepted the type of fight Navarrete wanted. Charly Suarez provided a more revealing test. His timing, movement, and cleaner punching gave Navarrete serious trouble before the bout ended because of a cut. Navarrete initially received a technical decision, but the California State Athletic Commission overturned the result to a no contest in June 2025.

He arguably deserved to lose and should already be settling that controversy in a rematch. The three-belt fight with Foster offers considerably more money and prestige, along with an understandable reason to leave Suarez behind.

Foster presents a harder tactical problem. He uses lateral movement to control distance and counters sharply when opponents sacrifice their balance. Navarrete routinely does exactly that while launching looping punches from unusual angles. That approach still carries danger for Foster. He has encountered trouble when opponents trap him against the ropes and deny him room to reset. Navarrete must attack the body and smother Foster’s space rather than waste punches chasing his head.

The WBC champion also has to make his cleaner work unmistakable. Navarrete’s activity and forward movement can influence judges even when many of his punches miss. Close rounds may become difficult to win if Foster spends long stretches defending without answering.

The crowd should favor Navarrete in San Antonio, but Foster has already defeated Stephen Fulton at Frost Bank Center. The surroundings will be familiar, even if the support is not.

Navarrete wants to turn the contest into a test of toughness and output. Foster intends to make it a test of precision, one in which his opponent’s former size edge will no longer rescue him.

Sports.title: Austin Williams Tests Vito Mielnicki’s Contender Claims
Sports.content:
Gardzielik was dropped and lost every round on all three scorecards. Nmomah offered limited resistance before being stopped in the ninth. Huerta went the distance but lost 100-90, 100-90, and 99-91. Those victories showed Mielnicki can dominate carefully selected opposition. They did not demonstrate that he is prepared for a championship fight.

Top Rank moved Mielnicki methodically by matching him against fighters with attractive records but little recognition in the United States. The approach helped him collect regional belts and climb the sanctioning-body rankings without facing anyone near the top of the middleweight class.

The more revealing performances came against Khalil El Harraz and Connor Coyle. Mielnicki edged El Harraz by majority decision and then struggled to a majority draw with Coyle. The New York State Athletic Commission later changed the Coyle result to a no-contest after he tested positive for performance-enhancing drugs, but the ruling did not erase what happened during those 10 rounds.

Mielnicki believes beating Williams would answer criticism of rankings that place him No. 3 with the WBO, No. 7 with the WBA and WBC, and No. 9 with the IBF.

“I feel like having a name like him on my resume will silence a lotta that,” Mielnicki told Keith Idec of The Ring.

Williams (20-2, 13 KOs) is a considerable upgrade. The physically strong southpaw applies pressure and can make Mielnicki fight while moving backward, an area that the trio was not equipped to test. Mielnicki must show that his footwork and inside game hold up when an opponent closes the distance and refuses to remain at his preferred pace.

Still, beating Williams would not establish Mielnicki as one of the best at 160. Hamzah Sheeraz stopped Williams, and Carlos Adames defeated him decisively over 12 rounds. Williams occupies the middle of the first tier: capable enough to expose a protected contender, but well below the elite.

That makes him an appropriate screening test. A Mielnicki loss in his New Jersey backyard would make his lofty rankings difficult to defend. A convincing win would earn him the opportunity to face the leading middleweights, not prove he is ready to beat them.

Sports.title: Hearn Disputes Kremlev’s Bivol-Beterbiev Trilogy Offer Claim
Sports.content:
“It was never offered, by the way,” said Hearn during a media scrum reported by ProBox TV . “If there was an offer that was even remotely reasonable, the Callum Smith fight wouldn’t be happening. Dmitry would have vacated and fought Beterbiev.”

That version is difficult to reconcile with Kremlev’s account. The IBA president said negotiations had taken place with both camps and that Bivol was offered twice his previous purse. Kremlev also claimed Beterbiev was willing to box without taking a purse to help complete the trilogy.

The dispute may come down to the difference between vocal backing and an actionable contract. A public promise of enormous money is not the same as written terms containing a date, venue, broadcaster, payment schedule, guarantees, and regulatory responsibilities.

Beterbiev’s reported willingness to compete for free demonstrates his desire for the fight, but it does not provide a workable economic structure. His purse was only one part of the proposed event. Someone still had to guarantee Bivol’s money and cover the considerable production and promotional costs.

Mandatory obligations have also dismantled the undisputed championship created by their first two fights. Bivol relinquished the WBC belt rather than defend against David Benavidez, then satisfied his IBF requirement. Facing Smith under the WBO order would place another challenger between Bivol and the trilogy.

Smith provides a useful common opponent. Beterbiev stopped him in seven rounds in January 2024, overpowering the former super middleweight champion with sustained pressure. A clear Bivol victory would invite comparisons, although their contrasting styles make a direct measurement unreliable. Beterbiev broke Smith physically; Bivol would be more likely to dismantle him through distance, timing, and combinations.

Delay carries a heavier price for Beterbiev. He has not fought since losing the rematch in February 2025, while Bivol returned against Michael Eifert and is preparing for Smith. At 41, Beterbiev cannot recover lost time through another training camp.

If the trilogy is postponed until 2027, Beterbiev may have spent nearly two years outside the ring. The eventual fight would still sell, but it might no longer settle the rivalry under conditions resembling their first two meetings. What began as a 50-50 conclusion risks becoming a test of how much age and inactivity have taken from Beterbiev.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Admits Early Success Cost Him Against Daniel Dubois
Sports.content:
“I felt a bit too comfortable maybe with the really early knockdown, then followed by another one in the third,” Wardley said during the kick-off press conference. “I thought this is near on a foregone conclusion. I’ve done it once, I’ve done it twice, I can get him out of there. “I was a victim of my own success in them early stages. I just got trigger-happy, got carried away with trying to launch that right hand. In the moments when I did have him hurt, I don’t actually think I jumped on him enough.”

The mistake was not simply failing to throw enough punches. Wardley stopped disguising the right hand and began loading up from too far away. Dubois steadied himself behind a stiff jab, controlled the distance, and forced him to expend more energy each time he attempted to close the space.

The challenger needs greater variety in London. Hooks to the ribs would give Dubois something else to consider behind his tight guard, while doubling the lead hook may create a cleaner route for Wardley’s power. Hunting for one spectacular shot only makes his attack easier to read.

Pacing will be just as important. An early knockdown does not require an immediate all-out assault, particularly in a fight scheduled for 12 rounds. Wardley must allow his successes to count on the scorecards without emptying his energy reserves in search of a dramatic finish.

The five-month turnaround adds another concern. Wardley absorbed sustained punishment before the 11th-round stoppage and has gone directly into another demanding camp without an interim bout. He dismissed questions about his condition, saying he had “absolutely zero excuses” for the defeat or the rematch.

Dubois carries the psychological advantage. He knows he can withstand Wardley’s heaviest punches, regain command with his jab, and break him down over the later rounds. The harder mental test for Wardley may arrive if he lands cleanly again and the champion refuses to fold.

The first fight established that Wardley can hurt Dubois. On October 17, he must show that early success will sharpen his decisions instead of distorting them.

Sports.title: Janibek Corners Hamzah Sheeraz Before WBO Deadline
Sports.content:
Sheeraz has already built a possible defense for refusing the fight. During an appearance on The Ariel Helwani Show, he called the WBO’s ruling a “joke” and criticized the organization for rewarding Janibek after his positive test for meldonium.

The clean-sport objection has merit. The WBO shortened Janibek’s suspension, allowed him to move directly into a mandatory position at 168 pounds, and selected him over Jacob Bank despite Janibek never fighting in the division. Bank had actively campaigned at super middleweight and petitioned for the same opportunity.

Still, Sheeraz’s moral position also provides a convenient exit. He can vacate while claiming he refused to cooperate with a sanctioning body order he considers disgraceful, rather than admitting that Janibek presents too much danger for too little money.

Surrendering the title would harm Sheeraz’s reputation. He won the vacant belt against 39-year-old Alem Begic and struggled through a majority verdict over Simon Zachenhuber in his first defense. Leaving before facing Janibek would support the Kazakh’s claim that Sheeraz was only a “champion by name.”

Facing Janibek carries the greater career risk. He is a precise southpaw counterpuncher with the power to punish the defensive lapses Sheeraz showed against Zachenhuber. A decisive loss would cost Sheeraz his belt and reduce his value for larger fights against Canelo Alvarez or Chris Eubank Jr.

The history makes an escape harder to disguise. Sheeraz withdrew from negotiations when the WBO ordered him to challenge Janibek at middleweight. After Sheeraz moved to 168 and became champion, Janibek followed him into the division.

Vacating can be presented as a principled business choice. Getting stopped by the opponent who pursued him through two weight classes would be far worse. Janibek has left Sheeraz to choose which consequence he is willing to accept.

Sports.title: Two Minutes in Tokyo: George Foreman Slaughters José Roman
Sports.content:
Roman had little chance of testing him. The Puerto Rican challenger stood 5-foot-10 and weighed between 196½ and 197 pounds, leaving him considerably smaller than the 6-foot-4, 219-pound champion. He had been outside the rankings when the fight was signed before being elevated to No. 9 by the WBA and WBC.

That placement gave the promotion official legitimacy, but it did not make Roman a genuine threat. Foreman was 38-0 with 35 knockouts and had just destroyed Frazier in two rounds to seize the championship. Roman brought a 43-7-1 or 44-7-1 record, depending on the source, with 21 knockouts.

Once the bell rang, even two minutes proved too long.

Foreman did not merely follow Roman and swing wildly. Under trainer Dick Sadler, he had learned to take broad lateral steps that closed escape routes. His lead hand served as more than a jab. He posted it against Roman, pushed him off balance, and turned him toward the right hand.

That rough leverage helped Foreman control opponents before the power punches landed. Some of it crossed into boxing’s gray area, particularly when he shoved or extended his lead arm, but Roman lacked the strength and composure to resist it.

The destruction of Frazier also followed Foreman into the ring. Roman knew that six knockdowns had reduced the previous champion to a helpless target. His tense movement and reluctance to commit gave Foreman little reason to respect anything coming back.

Foreman cut down the available space, drove Roman toward the ropes, and attacked his body. Roman fell along the ropes near the one-minute point, but referee Jay Edson initially treated it as a slip or loss of balance rather than a knockdown.

The decision became controversial when Foreman landed a right while Roman was sitting on the canvas. Roman’s manager, Bill Daly, and trainer, Al Braverman, jumped onto the apron demanding a disqualification. Edson ruled that Foreman had been following through and that the punch carried little force. Because the original fall was ruled a slip, Roman received neither a mandatory count nor additional recovery time.

The challenger rose, only to be dropped by a right hand. Roman made it up once more, but Foreman finished him with a right uppercut at exactly 2:00 of the opening round. Roman’s corner later called Foreman “the dirtiest fighter in the world,” while some members of the Tokyo crowd booed the abrupt ending.

Roman’s ranking exposed the business behind the defense. He was outside the WBA and WBC ratings when the fight was arranged, then elevated to No. 9 so the organizations could approve him as a challenger. The placement did not make him a mandatory contender or establish championship credentials. It allowed an overseas title defense to proceed against an opponent selected for limited risk.

Promoters advertised Foreman’s purse as $1 million, a figure that became attached to the fight in later records. Contemporary reporting placed his actual guarantee near $250,000, while other accounts and Foreman’s later recollections put his earnings in the $250,000 to $300,000 range. Roman received approximately $100,000.

Attendance reached roughly 7,500 to 8,000 in an arena capable of holding nearly twice that number. The midday Saturday scheduling and expensive tickets hurt local sales, leaving Japanese promoters braced for a financial loss despite televising the bout free to domestic viewers.

Foreman followed the Roman destruction by stopping Ken Norton in two rounds the next year. Across the Frazier, Roman, and Norton fights, he needed only five rounds to dispose of three heavyweights who had a combined 91 professional victories.

The two-minute result also concealed a flaw that Muhammad Ali later exploited. Foreman committed heavily to his power punches and expected resistance to collapse under the first sustained attack. Roman rewarded that approach by folding almost immediately.

Ali refused to provide the same response in Zaire the following year. He forced Foreman to keep punching after the quick finish failed to materialize, turning the champion’s aggression and confidence in his strength into an exhausting trap.

Foreman’s comeback decades later produced one of boxing’s greatest stories, capped by the heavyweight championship at age 45. Yet the older Foreman relied more on patience, positioning, and conservation. The 1973 version brought something more frightening: youth, crushing strength, and an appetite for immediate destruction.

Roman was never equipped to disprove it.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Says Crawford Resents His Boxing Takeover
Sports.content:
“I gave my honest opinion, saying that he left a lot on the table. That’s all I said. Crawford is the one that’s always coming up and slightly hating on me little by little. In the meantime, you’re retired. You should be in Turks and Caicos chilling on a yacht, enjoying your family. He’s desperate, bro,” said Ryan to Fight Hub TV. “Nobody knows him outside of boxing, so he’s doing everything he can to continue his name. He actually likes the attention. I used to think Crawford didn’t, but now I know he does. He realized nobody cares after you retire.”

Ryan also dismissed Crawford’s presence at Benn’s gym. “I feel like I’ll beat your ass, so what are you going to teach him?” he said.

Their bad blood highlights the fundamental difference between the two men. Crawford pursued championships, pound-for-pound recognition, and technical supremacy. Garcia measures his position through audience size, financial leverage, and the ability to command boxing’s most valuable dates.

Crawford built the greater traditional legacy, but Ryan attracts the larger mainstream audience. If Garcia defeats Benn and becomes boxing’s leading commercial figure, he will have achieved something Crawford never managed despite accomplishing far more inside the ring.

Working with Benn does not necessarily prove Garcia’s accusation that Crawford craves attention. It may represent a retired fighter transferring his knowledge to another contender. Garcia has turned that mentorship into an insult, reducing Benn to a pupil who cannot be saved even by one of boxing’s finest technicians.

That approach also keeps Benn’s abilities outside the discussion. By treating the fight as a proxy battle with Crawford, Garcia portrays him as little more than the vehicle for another man’s resentment.

The claim brings considerable risk. Garcia’s argument carries force only if he beats Benn. A loss would damage his attempt to place drawing power above championships while giving Crawford every reason to question both his boxing and his self-appointed status.

The message was simple: Crawford had his run and should either return to face someone such as Jaron Ennis or Vergil Ortiz Jr. or stay quiet in retirement.

Ghana News.title: Gauff’s flaw forgotten on winning US Open return
Ghana News.content:
The sight of a forlorn Coco Gauff hitting serves in the rain on the US Open practice courts became the defining image of her struggles last year.

The serving yips were undermining the two-time major champion's talent. Staying out in the persistent drizzle was a sign of how desperate she had become to iron out the major flaw in her game.

Twelve months on, the 22-year-old American has returned to the US Open with a rejuvenated service game - and it was the bedrock of her 6-3 6-4 win over Turkey's Zeynep Sonmez in the New York first round on Tuesday.

Gauff starting with a swift hold to love set the tone for a dominant first set, then used her opening shot to get her out of trouble when Sonmez threatened to go a break up in the second set.

"Now it's like I can look back a year on and think, 'Oh, wow, it's a big difference'," said Gauff, who is seeded fourth at Flushing Meadows this year.

"It feels good to come into a tournament feeling confident on that shot finally."

On the eve of her home Slam last year, Gauff decided to reshuffle her coaching team and hired biomechanics expert Gavin MacMillan - who helped four-time major champion Aryna Sabalenka overcome serving troubles earlier in her career.

It was a drastic move. But one which Gauff felt was unavoidable after hitting a high amount of double faults at the preceding Cincinnati Open.

Tweaking technique heading into the US Open - where she receives frenzied attention - was always going to be a risk.

So it was no surprise when Gauff suffered a fourth-round exit in a tournament where she looked fraught throughout and was reduced to tears during matches.

"Obviously last year I knew all the eyes were going to be on the serve," Gauff said.

"Gavin is so great at what he does, I felt a lot of pressure to kind of prove that. It didn't really show within the first two weeks, which is normal."

That was then. Now Gauff possesses a serve which is a serious weapon - even though she still leaks some double faults.

Showing greater consistency on the toss, not throwing the ball too far in front and keeping her wrist straighter have been MacMillan's pointers for a more reliable serve.

Gauff has hit a total of 301 double faults on the WTA Tour this season - more than any other player - although her average of 5.6 per match is lower than many of her peers

It was a key factor in her charge to the Cincinnati Open title earlier this month.

Analysis from that tournament showed how Gauff is hitting closer to the line but still maintaining her serve speed - underlining a significant improvement in her accuracy.

Gauff now has full confidence her serve can be too hot for opponents to handle - and it showed immediately against Sonmez.

The opening game saw Gauff thump a 112mph ace down the middle, followed by an unreturned first serve and another ace, on her way to holding serve in less than 90 seconds.

Sonmez struggled to get balls into play whenever Gauff landed a first serve in the first set, with the world number four winning 93% of those points.

Gauff broke again for a 1-0 lead in the second set, but her serve was not as effective as Sonmez levelled at 2-2 and held three more break points for a 4-2 lead.

But a precise ace out wide and a 115mph unreturned first serve enabled Gauff to cling on in a game which you felt she would have lost a year ago.

The gutsy hold laid the platform for Gauff to immediately break for 4-3 before securing victory with another service game which displayed her belief.

Gauff hit a trio of unreturned first serves - all just under the 120mph mark, teeing up three match points as Sonmez buckled on the first after a short rally.

"Psychologically, I'm now going to go for the ace, or I know I can hit the serve and the return is probably not going to come back," said Gauff, who will play Spain's Paula Badosa or Australia's Daria Kasatkina in the second round.

"Last year I literally was like I hope I make it in. It's such a big difference knowing almost every serve I'm trying to basically hit 110, 115, 120mph if I can."

Ghana News.title: Birds stop play but Medvedev flies into third round
Ghana News.content:
An interruption from a pair of birds ruffled Daniil Medvedev's feathers but could not disrupt the seventh seed as he eased into the US Open third round with a dominant victory over Sebastian Gorzny.

The two birds settled down on the net for a closer look at the action midway through a second-set rally, with play continuing around them for several strokes before the chair umpire called for the point to be replayed.

Medvedev, who ranked the incident among his "top five" most unusual experiences at the New York major, was visibly stunned by the decision, which came just after he thought he had won the point with a cross-court forehand.

"This is very bad," the 2021 champion said as he remonstrated at the umpire on court.

Image caption,The two birds sat either side of the centre line to watch the action

Russia's Medvedev is no stranger to losing his composure on court, notably receiving a fine of almost £31,500 at last year's US Open for an extraordinary meltdown during his first-round defeat to Benjamin Bonzi.

As recently as last month's Winston-Salem Open, where he again lost in the opening round, he spent a disconsolate change of ends questioning his future in the sport, musing "maybe I should start a career in pickleball".

However, the 30-year-old, who had already flown through the first set in just 21 minutes, quickly brushed aside the avian interruption to complete a straightforward 6-1 6-3 7-5 win over American wildcard Gorzny, the world number 731.

"I saw [the birds] straight away," Medvedev - who will play Frenchman Arthur Rinderknech in the third round - said in his on-court interview.

"I thought the point would stop straight away but it didn't.

"Then we play for 45 seconds and the moment I hit the winner we say stop. I'm like, 'Why? We played for 45 seconds!'.

"But it's okay. I was not happy with the decision but it is was it is. You can't do anything with it.

"The situation was pretty crazy but I love this court, I'm happy to win, to stay in the US Open, to stay in New York for longer."

Gorzny was making his Grand Slam debut at the US Open, seven years after being given a 5% chance to live after being taken ill at the USTA Boys' 16s National Championships in Michigan.

Then aged 15, Gorzny suffered a seizure in the night and was placed in an induced coma for four days.

"The doctors aren't really sure what it was actually, but they're guessing a mosquito bite that led to some type of brain infection: meningitis, encephalitis," Gorzny told the ATP before the US Open.

A former Wimbledon boys' doubles champion, Gorzny, the world number 731, earned his place in the main draw at Flushing Meadows by winning the USTA American Collegiate Player Wildcard Playoff in June.

Ghana News.title: LA Clippers fined $30m by NBA over Leonard scandal
Ghana News.content:
The LA Clippers have been fined $30m (£22.2m) by the National Basketball Association (NBA) for violating salary rules in order to funnel millions of dollars to star player Kawhi Leonard.

The fine - the largest in the league's history - comes after the NBA report said Leonard pressured the Clippers into "obtaining off-court income opportunities [and] successfully obtaining those opportunities".

The Clippers will also have to forfeit five first-round draft picks between 2029 and 2033, while owner Steve Ballmer has been suspended from all league and team activities for 12 months for his role in matters involving Leonard's sponsorship contracts during his time with the franchise.

The NBA said the Clippers had been guilty of "knowingly seeking to help Mr Leonard obtain off-court income opportunities".

NBA commissioner Adam Silver said he was "deeply disappointed" by the Clippers' "flagrant violations" of the rules and said he believed the "severity of the penalties reflects the seriousness of the violations".

Two-time NBA champion Leonard has been fined $700,000 (£518,997) by the league.

The team's president of business operations, Gillian Zucker, has been suspended for one year without pay for providing "misleading statements to investigators".

The punishments come after the NBA said its month-long investigation "found a pattern of misconduct and multiple significant rules violations by the Clippers organisation, a prior offender of the salary-cap circumvention rules".

Following the ruling, Leonard, 35, said he "accepts full responsibility" for his actions and "regrets the distraction this situation has caused the fans and my family".

"I entered into my contract with the Clippers as well as the agreements in question in good faith, fully committed to fulfilling my obligations and with no knowledge of any intent on anyone's part to circumvent the salary cap," he wrote on Instagram.

The two-time NBA Finals MVP joined the Clippers in 2019 and spent seven years with the franchise before leaving earlier this year.

The NBA said both the "organisation and personnel" of the Clippers will be subject to a compliance and monitoring programme overseen by the league for five years.

Ghana News.title: Uber to cut over 3,000 jobs in major global restructuring
Ghana News.content:
Uber is cutting more than 3,000 jobs worldwide as part of a major overhaul designed to shrink management layers and refocus spending on its core business.

The cuts amount to roughly 10% of its global workforce, bringing staffing back to levels last seen in 2021.

Chief executive Dara Khosrowshahi told staff in a company email that the taxi and delivery firm had expanded quickly but had accumulated too many layers and small teams, which slowed decision‑making.

He said the reductions would put Uber, which has its global head office in San Francisco, US, in a better position for its "biggest opportunities ahead of us".

The move marks one of Uber's largest restructurings in years and signals a shift towards a leaner operating model.

Shares rose nearly 2% after the announcement, with investors appearing to welcome the proposals.

Cuts affect both managers and non-managers, and Uber said it plans to fold many of its smallest teams into larger groups, however, the firm has not confirmed the locations most affected by job cuts.

Such changes are intended to make Uber "simpler" and "faster," while freeing up money to reinvest in areas it considers central to its future, Khosrowshahi said.

The restructuring comes as Uber steps up investment in autonomous vehicle partnerships and expands its ride‑hailing, delivery, and robotaxi operations.

Uber is also tightening up its office strategy, asking nearly all employees to work in person at designated hubs and limiting remote roles to about 1%.

Analysts said the layoffs could generate up to $2bn in annual savings.

Unlike many large technology companies that have cut jobs amid heavy spending on artificial intelligence (AI), Uber had avoided major reductions since the pandemic.

The latest changes bring its workforce back to just under 30,000 people, roughly where it stood before its most recent period of expansion.

Ghana News.title: Tiger Woods gets five-year driving ban after reckless driving plea
Ghana News.content:
Tiger Woods has agreed not to contest a reckless driving charge as part of a deal with prosecutors, reducing the original charge of driving under the influence from a rollover crash in Florida.

The golfer accepted a five-year suspension of his driving licence and a $1,000 (£742) fine, as part of a plea agreement with prosecutors in Martin County, Florida.

Woods was arrested after the March crash and had passed a breathalyser test but declined further testing for other drugs.

He pleaded not guilty the same month to misdemeanour charges of driving under the influence and refusal to submit to testing. Woods, 50, said he was seeking treatment after the incident.

"I'm completely confident and comfortable with the resolution of this case," Florida State Attorney Thomas Bakkedahl said at a press conference after the hearing.

He said he strove to treat Woods like any other defendant.

"Today I resolved case involving a man who drives a golf ball for a living," Bakkedahl said. "Tomorrow, I'll resolve a case in the same matter for a man who drives a nail for a living."

No one was injured in the crash, though Woods had to crawl out through the passenger door to free himself.

Police released body camera footage in April that captured the aftermath of the incident, showing the golfing legend after his vehicle clipped a truck and rolled over.

In the video, Woods appears calm, kneeling on one knee as he tells officers: "I looked down at my phone, and all of a sudden, boom".

He passed a breathalyser test but declined to take a urinalysis screening for other drugs, Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said at the time.

Woods told officers he had not consumed alcohol that day. When asked about any prescription medication, he responded, "I take a few", adding he had done so earlier that morning.

He then listed the medication, though that portion of the footage was redacted.

Officers told Woods they suspected his "normal faculties" were impaired by an "unknown substance".

Authorities later reported finding two white pills in his pocket, identified as hydrocodone, an opioid commonly prescribed to treat pain.

Woods wrote on social media following the incident, "I know and understand the seriousness of the situation I find myself in today.

"I am stepping away for a period of time to seek treatment and focus on my health. This is necessary in order for me to prioritise my wellbeing and work toward lasting recovery."

The incident marked Woods' second arrest on suspicion of driving under the influence.

Ghana News.title: South African airline behind daring stadium stunt cancels next flyby
Ghana News.content:
The South African airline behind a stunt which saw two planes flying in close formation low over a packed stadium has cancelled a similar operation this weekend.

Airlink confirmed it had withdrawn its application for the display set to take place before South Africa's rugby match with New Zealand in Johannesburg on Saturday, citing a poor weather forecast.

The airline's flying feat divided opinion, with some labelling the startling manoeuvre reckless while others praised the precision and expertise.

It comes as the country's aviation regulator said that while it had approved the application for the flyby, it was now reviewing the operation following "discussions in the media".

Footage of last weekend's air show before the start of the match in Cape Town was shared around the world.

Flight tracking website Flightradar24 said that according to its analysis "the lead aircraft passed less than 50ft (15m) above the top of the stadium".

From some angles the jets appeared very close to the roof of the DHL Stadium as they roared over amid coloured flare smoke.

The South African Civil Aviation Authority (SACAA) said on Wednesday it would review the incident.

"Following various discussions in the media relating to the events of the past weekend, the SACAA initiated compliance verifications, engaged the operator, obtained the Flight Data Recording downloads as well as other additional requirements," it said in a statement.

It also revealed that a flight simulator used to practice for the Saturday flight was used as part of the approvals process.

In a separate statement on Wednesday, the airline confirmed the display planned for the upcoming weekend would not go ahead.

"Although we have also heard the widespread enthusiasm for a flyby at FNB Stadium this weekend, the forecast weather points to unfavourable conditions for a safe formation flyby," CEO de Villiers Engelbrecht said.

He said last weekend's flights were conducted at "approved and rehearsed safety altitude and speed limits for the flypast" and by a "highly experienced crew".

Airlink said that it had volunteered to provide the aircraft's digital flight data recordings following "unprecedented public interest" in the flyby.

The airline said it was "grateful for the enthusiastic appreciation" people had expressed in response, but also noted "the valid questions and concerns raised".

"We never intended to become the news or upstage Rugby's Greatest Rivalry," Engelbrecht added.

The flyby has been a feature at major sporting and presidential events in South Africa several times over the years - using both military jets and commercial airlines.

Ghana News.title: PURC urges ECG to address outages, metering delays
Ghana News.content:
The Public Utilities Regulatory Commission (PURC) has urged the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) to address persistent power outages and delays in the acquisition and replacement of meters.

The Commission said the concerns were among the major issues raised during its mid-year monitoring and consumer engagements across the Greater Accra Region.

Madam Gifty Bruce-Nelson, Greater Accra Regional Manager at PURC, made the call during a meeting with ECG district managers and technical officers from the region’s district offices.

She said the engagement was aimed at strengthening collaboration between the two institutions and providing firsthand information on operational, technical, and customer service challenges affecting electricity supply.

Madam Bruce-Nelson said the region recorded the highest number of complaints about electricity service quality during the mid-year review, mainly involving persistent outages, phase-offs, power fluctuations and low voltages.

She said the Commission’s electronic complaint channels, including its WhatsApp platforms, had facilitated the reporting of consumer concerns, while field and industrial monitoring had identified overloaded transformers, meter shortages and theft, network connectivity gaps and instances of impersonation of ECG staff.

Madam Bruce-Nelson urged ECG to prioritise transformer upgrades and network infrastructure improvements, to improve communication with consumers on fault restoration, and to strengthen field operations.

She also called for greater efficiency in the acquisition, installation, and replacement of meters, saying that delays contributed to estimated billing, illegal connections, and disputes over electricity consumption.

“Kindly improve the efficiency of the metering process and provide consumers with clear information regarding application procedures, requirements and expected timelines,” she said.

Billing was also identified as a major source of consumer complaints, including concerns over high electricity bills, meter-reading problems, delays in resolving billing disputes and discrepancies between expected and actual consumption.

Some ECG district managers said some customers had installed substandard meters that were not captured in the company’s system and had subsequently refused to pay their bills.

They said community engagements had therefore been organised to educate consumers on the need to pay their bills and ensure that all meters were properly captured in the ECG system.

The managers also cited the transition to a new billing system following the shutdown of the previous one as a factor contributing to some billing challenges.

Issues relating to SHEP meters and the distribution of meters outside ECG’s regular systems were also discussed.

The engagement was part of PURC and ECG's efforts to strengthen collaboration and improve electricity service delivery and customer relations in the region.

Ghana News.title: Police engage traders over alleged harassment, extortion on Aflao-Accra highway
Ghana News.content:
The Volta Regional Police Command has engaged traders and market women in parts of the Southern Volta Region to hear their concerns following allegations of harassment and extortion by some police officers stationed along the Aflao-Accra highway.

The engagement, led by Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCOP) Wisdom Akorli, Volta Regional Police Commander, was part of the Command's efforts to obtain first-hand information from traders and other road users about their experiences with police personnel along the highway.

The exercise followed a petition by Mr Daniel Jerry Sorokpo, a youth activist and aspiring NDC Vice Chairman of the Ketu South Constituency, to the Inspector-General of Police (IGP), Christian Tetteh Yohunu, over alleged harassment and extortion of traders transporting goods along the corridor.

Following the petition, the IGP invited the Volta Regional Police Commander to Accra to discuss the concerns raised, after which the Regional Commander and his team embarked on an outreach exercise to engage traders and hear their experiences firsthand.

The team started the engagement at Sogakope and proceeded through Akatsi and Agbozume before reaching Aflao, where traders had the opportunity to raise concerns about their encounters with police personnel on the highway.

Chief Inspector Francis Kwaku Gomado, Volta Regional Police Public Relations Officer, told the media that the exercise was intended to enable the Command to understand the issues on the ground and take appropriate steps to address any misconduct identified.

He said the Command had received reports alleging that some police officers along the Aflao-Accra highway were harassing traders and demanding money from them while they transported goods.

Chief Inspector Gomado stressed that police officers had no authority to demand money from traders or other road users simply because they were transporting goods.

He also expressed concern about reports that some traders and travellers were detained for several hours along the highway, describing such conduct as unacceptable.

The Regional Police PRO urged members of the public who experienced harassment, extortion or other forms of misconduct by police personnel to report directly to the Regional Police Commander or his deputies for investigation.

He advised the public to note officers who failed to properly display their names on their uniforms and to report such cases to the appropriate authorities.

According to the petition, traders transporting commodities such as rice, sugar, cooking oil, beans, and vegetables were sometimes stopped by police officers and asked to produce receipts for their goods.

It alleged that traders who were unable to produce the required receipts were sometimes compelled to pay money to the officers.

Some market women who interacted with the Police team also confirmed the allegations, claiming that some officers demanded amounts of not less than GH¢50 from them.

They said such demands were sometimes made even when they were transporting goods from their homes to nearby local markets.

The traders, however, expressed appreciation to the Regional Police Command for engaging with them directly and listening to their concerns.

They said the exercise was important in helping the Police understand the challenges faced by traders and could help restore confidence between the two groups.

Mr Sorokpo, in his petition to the IGP, called for a thorough investigation into the allegations and for appropriate action against any police officer found to have acted unlawfully or abused their authority.

The engagement is expected to provide the Police Command with first-hand accounts from traders and other road users and assist in identifying areas requiring further investigation and action along the Aflao-Accra corridor.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: OpenAI faces new lawsuits over Tumbler Ridge mass shooting tragedy
World.content:
Multiple new cases have been filed against OpenAI, alleging ChatGPT played a role in the Tumbler Ridge mass shooting.

OpenAI is facing another wave of lawsuits in the wake of the February mass shooting in Tumbler Ridge in Canada’s province of British Columbia, which left eight people dead.

On Wednesday, 30 new complaints were reportedly filed in a United States federal court in California, including teachers and students who were witnesses and survivors at the school where most of the shooting took place, joining seven initial lawsuits filed in April.

The lawsuits accuse the San Francisco, California-based artificial intelligence giant and its CEO, Sam Altman, of negligence, as well as aiding and abetting a mass shooting.

The suits, brought by lawyer Jay Edelson, allege that the company knew about the intentions of the 18-year-old shooter who, in her interactions with OpenAI’s chatbot ChatGPT, had described scenarios involving gun violence, but that the leadership did not report their concerns to law enforcement, echoing earlier lawsuits on the matter.

In April, Altman penned a letter to the community apologising that the company did not alert law enforcement about the shooter, Jesse Van Rootselaar.

“While I know words can never be enough, I believe an apology is necessary to recognize the harm and irreversible loss your community has suffered,” Altman wrote in the letter.

Authorities say that Van Rootselaar killed her mother and half-brother before going to the Tumbler Ridge Secondary School and opening fire. Five children and one educator were killed at the school. More than 25 others were wounded before Van Rootselaar died from what police described as a self-inflicted gunshot wound.



One of the new cases filed was on behalf of a 13-year-old identified as A C, who played dead after watching the shooter kill their classmates and the teacher. Another new case was brought by a grade seven teacher named Deidre Rushlow, who hid under her desk with her students during the rampage.

“There isn’t a day that goes by that I don’t think about what happened at Tumbler Ridge, or the victims of this devastating tragedy and their families. It’s a constant and sobering reminder of the important and incredibly difficult work that many people in my team do each and every day,” Jason Kwon, OpenAI’s head of strategy, wrote in a post on X on Wednesday.

“We’ve been approaching this litigation with respect for both the legal process and the families and victims of this tragedy, and we’ll continue to engage in good faith with that process.”

Edelson did not respond to Al Jazeera’s request for comment.

Growing legal pressure

In July, British Columbia’s Attorney General Niki Sharma announced that the province would also pursue “all legal avenues to hold OpenAI and its decision-makers accountable” for the shooting.

The company has faced a growing slate of suits, apart from the ones from British Columbia, alleging that its product played a role in incidents that led to users harming others and themselves.

A recent lawsuit in Florida alleges that the company “actively assisted and encouraged the mass shooting” at Florida State University in April 2025.

There are other complaints filed on behalf of victims across the US and Canada alleging that the victims took their own lives after being pushed by ChatGPT to do so, including a case in Quebec earlier this year.

World.title: Republican senator calls on Trump to fire Secretary of Defence Hegseth
World.content:
Senator Thom Tillis accuses Pentagon chief of ‘inept mismanagement’ as US military is strained by war on Iran.

Share Republican senator calls on Trump to fire Secretary of Defence Hegseth on social media

United States Senator Thom Tillis has called on President Donald Trump to fire Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth for creating a “leadership void” within the military amid the ongoing war with Iran.

In a social media post on Wednesday, Tillis contrasted Hegseth unfavourably with former Army Secretary Dan Driscoll, who submitted his resignation on Monday amid reported disagreements with the Pentagon chief.

“I have never witnessed more inept management of the brave men and women who serve our country. He is intimidated by competence and retreats to ginning up culture wars instead of soberly attending to the vital work of our national defense and the health and well-being of our fighting force,” the North Carolina senator wrote.

“I urge the President to find a new leader at the Pentagon who will retain and empower our military talent rather than diminish it.”

Tillis is a member of Trump’s Republican Party. But in recent years, he has become an increasingly vocal critic from within the party over policies he fears harm democracy.

In June 2025, amid criticism from Trump, Tillis announced he would not be seeking re-election in November’s congressional midterm polls. His term ends in January.

Early in Trump’s second term as president, Tillis was among the senators who voted to confirm Hegseth, a military veteran and former TV host, despite criticisms of his conduct towards women and his past work.

Tillis only confirmed his vote in favour of Hegseth at the last minute, appearing to share some of the concerns being debated in the Senate.



Since taking office as defence secretary, Hegseth has pursued controversial changes to the Pentagon, including attempts to limit journalistic access to the Defence Department.

He has also undertaken a wide-ranging effort to root out what he calls “wokeness” from the military.

That effort has reportedly included firing top military leaders, blocking promotions, removing transgender service members and reviewing admissions standards for top military academies.

In Wednesday’s post, Tillis pointed to some of those efforts, questioning why Hegseth appeared fixated on culture war issues rather than modernising the military.

He pointed to evolving forms of warfare in Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, and in the US-Israeli war against Iran.

“Our understanding and assumptions of warfare are being challenged in places like Ukraine and Iran, and Dan [Driscoll] understands the old way of doing business no longer applies,” said Tillis.

The senator then proceeded to imply that Driscoll’s departure was a direct result of Hegseth’s mismanagement.

“If we had a Secretary of Defense who maintained the same priorities and forward-thinking, he would be fighting to retain talented leaders like Dan and the many flag officers he has forced into retirement. Instead, he is creating a leadership void at the top of our military ranks,” Tillis added.

Hegseth has faced growing scrutiny in recent months as the US struggles to achieve its goals in the war on Iran, launched on February 28. The war hit its six-month mark last week with no end in sight.

Media reports indicate that the war has left the Pentagon struggling with shrinking munitions stockpiles that could hinder the US military in future actions.

The war has also taken a toll on the popularity of the Trump administration, which has seen approval numbers sink ahead of the November congressional election.

Since the war began, fuel prices have skyrocketed, and the conflict has spread across the Middle East.

More than two-thirds of Americans disapprove of the administration’s handling of the war, according to a University of Massachusetts poll released on August 31.
